knowledge_statements.statement_title: Injection Criterion for Two Indexed Set Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes member-respecting injections by cardinality comparisons for all corresponding union-intersection expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_1,\ldots,A_n,B_1,\ldots,B_n\) be sets. There exists an injection \[f:\bigcup_{i=1}^n A_i\longrightarrow\bigcup_{i=1}^n B_i\] satisfying \(f[A_i]\subseteq B_i\) for every \(i\) if and only if every set obtained from \(A_1,\ldots,A_n\) by unions and intersections has cardinality at most that of the set obtained by applying the same operations to \(B_1,\ldots,B_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An injection from the union of the A-family to the union of the B-family that maps each Ai into the corresponding Bi exists exactly when every union-intersection construction from the A-sets is no larger than the corresponding construction from the B-sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ injective }f:\bigcup_{i=1}^nA_i\to\bigcup_{i=1}^nB_i\text{ with }f[A_i]\subseteq B_i\ \forall i\iff |E(A_1,\ldots,A_n)|\le|E(B_1,\ldots,B_n)|\text{ for every expression }E\text{ formed using unions and intersections}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint incidence in finite pairwise-intersecting families of d-intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d,n\ge 1\) be integers. For \(i=1,\ldots,n\), write \(J_i=\bigcup_{k=1}^d I_{ik}\), where each \(I_{ik}\) is a closed interval. If \(J_i\cap J_j\neq\varnothing\) for all \(i,j\), then an endpoint of some \(I_{ik}\) is contained in at least \(n/(2d)\) of the sets \(J_1,\ldots,J_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among n pairwise-intersecting d-intervals, some endpoint of a constituent closed interval lies in at least n/(2d) members of the family.
assumptions_latex: I_{ik}\text{ is a closed interval for every }i,k
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists i,k\ \exists x\in\partial I_{ik}:\ \left|\{j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:x\in J_j\}\right|\ge \frac{n}{2d}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses the minimum weight of a common transversal as an integer weight-splitting maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A=(A_1,\ldots,A_n)\) and \(\mathcal B=(B_1,\ldots,B_n)\) be families of subsets of \(S\), and let \(w:S\to\mathbb Z\). The minimum weight of a common transversal equals \[\max_{\substack{w_1,w_2\in\mathbb Z^S\\ w_1+w_2\ge w}}\left[\sum_{i=1}^n\left(\min_{s\in A_i}w_1(s)+\min_{s\in B_i}w_2(s)\right)+w(S)-w_1(S)-w_2(S)\right],\] where \(w_1+w_2\ge w\) is pointwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two families of n subsets of S with integer element weights, the minimum common-transversal weight equals the maximum of the stated weight-splitting expression over integer functions w1 and w2 whose pointwise sum dominates w.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A=(A_1,\ldots,A_n)\) and \(\mathcal B=(B_1,\ldots,B_n)\) are families of subsets of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{w(T):T\text{ is a common transversal}\}=\max_{\substack{w_1,w_2\in\mathbb Z^S\\w_1+w_2\ge w}}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n\left(\min_{s\in A_i}w_1(s)+\min_{s\in B_i}w_2(s)\right)+w(S)-w_1(S)-w_2(S)\right\}.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criterion for a common transversal containing a prescribed set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes existence of a common transversal required to contain a given subset, using the source notation \(A_I\) and \(B_J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A=(A_1,\ldots,A_n)\) and \(\mathcal B=(B_1,\ldots,B_n)\) be families of subsets of a set \(S\), and let \(X\subseteq S\). They have a common transversal containing \(X\) if and only if \[|A_I\cap B_J|\ge |I|+|J|-n+|X\setminus(A_I\cup B_J)|\] for all \(I,J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two families of n subsets of S have a common transversal containing X exactly when every pair of index subsets satisfies the stated inequality, including the correction for elements of X outside the corresponding unions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A=(A_1,\ldots,A_n)\) and \(\mathcal B=(B_1,\ldots,B_n)\) are families of subsets of a set \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\text{ a common transversal }T\supseteq X\iff (\forall I,J\subseteq[n])\ |A_I\cap B_J|\ge |I|+|J|-n+|X\setminus(A_I\cup B_J)|.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum Disjoint Packing of Sets Supporting Two Transversals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Here A_I=\bigcup_{i\in I}A_i and B_I=\bigcup_{i\in I}B_i. Within each S_r, the transversals of the two families may be different.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \mathcal A=(A_1,\ldots,A_n) and \mathcal B=(B_1,\ldots,B_n) be families of subsets of S. The maximum integer k for which there are pairwise disjoint subsets S_1,\ldots,S_k\subseteq S, each containing a transversal of \mathcal A and a transversal of \mathcal B, is
\[
\left\lfloor\min_{\varnothing\ne I\subseteq[n]}\min\left\{\frac{|A_I|}{|I|},\frac{|B_I|}{|I|}\right\}\right\rfloor.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum number of disjoint subsets that each support one transversal of each family equals the floor of the minimum stated union-size ratio. The two transversals within a subset need not be the same set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k_{\max}=\left\lfloor\min_{\varnothing\ne I\subseteq[n]}\min\left\{\frac{|A_I|}{|I|},\frac{|B_I|}{|I|}\right\}\right\rfloor

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hall's marriage theorem for set families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient condition for a finite indexed set family to possess a transversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A=(A_1,\ldots,A_n)\), and define \(A_I=\bigcup_{i\in I}A_i\). Then \(\mathcal A\) has a transversal if and only if \(|A_I|\ge |I|\) for every \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite indexed family has a system of distinct representatives exactly when the union of every subfamily contains at least as many elements as the subfamily has sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal A\text{ has a transversal}\iff \forall I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\},\ |A_I|\ge |I|

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \mathcal A=(A_1,\ldots,A_n) be a family of subsets of S, let a\in\mathbb Z_+^n, and let b\in\mathbb Z_+^S. There exist subsets B_i\subseteq A_i with |B_i|=a_i for all i, such that every s\in S belongs to at most b(s) of the sets B_i, if and only if
\[
b(X)+\sum_{i\in I}|A_i\setminus X|\geq a(I)
\]
for every X\subseteq S and every I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subsets of prescribed sizes can be selected from the indexed sets while respecting every element's occurrence capacity exactly when all ground-set and index-set subsets satisfy the stated inequality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criterion for Prescribed-Size Selections with Bounded Multiplicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes feasibility of equal-size selections subject to a uniform upper bound on element multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A=(A_1,\ldots,A_n)\) be a family of subsets of a set \(S\), and let \(r,s\in\mathbb Z_+\). There exist subsets \(B_i\subseteq A_i\) such that \(|B_i|=s\) for every \(i\) and each element of \(S\) belongs to at most \(r\) of the sets \(B_i\) if and only if, for every \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(X\subseteq S\), \[r|X|+\sum_{i\in I}|A_i\setminus X|\ge s|I|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subsets of size s can be selected from every indexed set so that each ground element occurs in at most r selections exactly when the stated inequality holds for every index set I and every subset X of the ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\exists B_i\subseteq A_i:\ |B_i|=s\ \forall i,\ |\{i:x\in B_i\}|\le r\ \forall x\in S\bigr)\iff\bigl(r|X|+\sum_{i\in I}|A_i\setminus X|\ge s|I|\ \forall I\subseteq[n],\ \forall X\subseteq S\bigr)

knowledge_statements.title: Covering–Packing Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary weak duality between integral set-system packing and transversal numbers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be finite, let \(\mathcal F\subseteq 2^E\) contain no empty set, and let \(\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal F\) be pairwise disjoint. Every transversal \(T\subseteq E\) contains at least one distinct element from each member of \(\mathcal P\); hence \(|\mathcal P|\le |T|\). Maximizing over disjoint packings and minimizing over transversals gives \[\nu(\mathcal F)\le\tau(\mathcal F).\] Equality is not guaranteed for an arbitrary set system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every transversal must select distinct representatives from pairwise disjoint members, so the maximum packing size never exceeds the minimum transversal size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nu(\mathcal F)\le\tau(\mathcal F)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Independence Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite hereditary set systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An independence system is a pair \((E,\mathcal I)\), where \(E\) is finite and \(\mathcal I\subseteq 2^E\), satisfying \(\varnothing\in\mathcal I\) and the hereditary axiom \[I\in\mathcal I,\ J\subseteq I\quad\Longrightarrow\quad J\in\mathcal I.\] Members of \(\mathcal I\) are independent sets. A set in \(2^E\setminus\mathcal I\) is dependent, and an inclusion-maximal member of \(\mathcal I\) is a maximal independent set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independence system is a finite family of feasible sets containing the empty set and closed under taking subsets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((E,\mathcal I)\) is an independence system exactly when \(\varnothing\in\mathcal I\) and \(\mathcal I\) is hereditary.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epsilon-Dominance of Sets in an Independence System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition combining approximate agreement of subset costs with approximate dominance among extending bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(E,\mathcal F)$ be an independence system, let $c:E\to\mathbb Z_+$, let $S_1,S_2\subseteq E$, and let $\epsilon>0$. Then $S_1$ $\epsilon$-dominates $S_2$ if $\frac{1}{1+\epsilon}c(S_1)\le c(S_2)\le(1+\epsilon)c(S_1)$ and there exists a basis $B_1$ of $(E,\mathcal F)$ with $S_1\subseteq B_1$ such that every basis $B_2$ with $S_2\subseteq B_2$ satisfies $(1+\epsilon)c(B_1)\ge c(B_2)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: S1 epsilon-dominates S2 when their costs differ by at most a factor 1+epsilon and some basis extending S1 has, up to that factor, at least the cost of every basis extending S2.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_1\succcurlyeq_\epsilon S_2\iff\left[\frac{c(S_1)}{1+\epsilon}\le c(S_2)\le(1+\epsilon)c(S_1)\right]\land\left[\exists B_1\supseteq S_1\ \forall B_2\supseteq S_2:\ (1+\epsilon)c(B_1)\ge c(B_2)\right].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank and Closure of an Independence System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines rank and closure for subsets of the ground set of an arbitrary independence system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(E,\mathcal F)$ be an independence system. For $X\subseteq E$, define
\[r(X):=\max\{|Y|:Y\subseteq X,\ Y\in\mathcal F\},\qquad \sigma(X):=\{y\in E:r(X\cup\{y\})=r(X)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rank of X is the maximum cardinality of an independent subset of X. Its closure consists of the ground-set elements whose addition does not increase that rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r(X)=\max\{|Y|:Y\subseteq X,\ Y\in\mathcal F\},\qquad \sigma(X)=\{y\in E:r(X\cup\{y\})=r(X)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower Rank and Rank Quotient of an Independence System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines lower rank and rank quotient for an independence system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(E,\mathcal F)$ be an independence system. For each $X\subseteq E$, define
\[
\rho(X):=\min\bigl\{|Y|:Y\subseteq X,\ Y\in\mathcal F,\text{ and }Y\cup\{x\}\notin\mathcal F\text{ for every }x\in X\setminus Y\bigr\}.
\]
The rank quotient is
\[
q(E,\mathcal F):=\min_{F\subseteq E}\frac{\rho(F)}{r(F)}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lower rank of X is the minimum cardinality of an independent subset that is maximal within X. The rank quotient is the minimum over subsets F of the ratio of lower rank to rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall X\subseteq E,\ \rho(X)=\min\{|Y|:Y\subseteq X,\ Y\in\mathcal F,\ \forall x\in X\setminus Y,\ Y\cup\{x\}\notin\mathcal F\},\qquad q(E,\mathcal F)=\min_{F\subseteq E}\frac{\rho(F)}{r(F)}

knowledge_statements.title: Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite matroids in independent-set form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid is a pair \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\), where \(E\) is finite and \(\mathcal I\subseteq 2^E\), such that \(\varnothing\in\mathcal I\), \(J\subseteq I\in\mathcal I\) implies \(J\in\mathcal I\), and the augmentation axiom holds: \[I,J\in\mathcal I,\ |I|<|J|\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \text{there exists }e\in J\setminus I\text{ with }I\cup\{e\}\in\mathcal I.\] The members of \(\mathcal I\) are the independent sets of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is a hereditary finite independence system in which every smaller independent set can be augmented toward a larger one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) is a matroid when heredity and augmentation hold.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independence-axiom definition of a finite matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid is a pair \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\), where \(E\) is finite and \(\mathcal I\subseteq 2^E\), such that: (I1) \(\varnothing\in\mathcal I\); (I2) if \(X\subseteq Y\in\mathcal I\), then \(X\in\mathcal I\); and (I3) if \(X,Y\in\mathcal I\) and \(|Y|>|X|\), then there exists \(e\in Y\setminus X\) such that \(X\cup\{e\}\in\mathcal I\). The members of \(\mathcal I\) are the independent sets, \(E\) is the ground set, and I3 is the exchange axiom.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite matroid consists of a finite ground set and a family of subsets containing the empty set, closed downward under inclusion, and satisfying the exchange axiom: any smaller independent set can be augmented by an element of a larger independent set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M=(E,\mathcal I)\text{ is a matroid if and only if axioms I1--I3 hold.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Augmentation and Basis-Cardinality Characterizations of Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the matroid exchange property through unit-gap augmentation and equicardinality of bases in every restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(E,\mathcal F)$ be an independence system. The following are equivalent: (i) for all $X,Y\in\mathcal F$ with $|X|>|Y|$, there exists $x\in X\setminus Y$ such that $Y\cup\{x\}\in\mathcal F$; (ii) the same conclusion holds whenever $|X|=|Y|+1$; (iii) for every $Z\subseteq E$, all inclusion-maximal independent subsets of $Z$ have the same cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an independence system, full augmentation, augmentation for independent sets whose sizes differ by one, and equal cardinality of all bases of every subset are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{(i)}\iff\mathrm{(ii)}\iff\mathrm{(iii)}.

children.title: Greedoids
children.top_down_role: Accessible feasible-set families with generalized exchange structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Greedoids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite greedoids in feasible-set form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A greedoid is a pair \((E,\mathcal F)\), where \(E\) is finite and \(\mathcal F\subseteq 2^E\), satisfying \(\varnothing\in\mathcal F\), accessibility, and augmentation. Accessibility requires that every nonempty \(X\in\mathcal F\) contain some \(x\in X\) with \(X\setminus\{x\}\in\mathcal F\). Augmentation requires \[X,Y\in\mathcal F,\ |X|<|Y|\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \text{there exists }y\in Y\setminus X\text{ with }X\cup\{y\}\in\mathcal F.\] The members of \(\mathcal F\) are feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite greedoid has the empty set as feasible, is accessible by single-element deletion, and satisfies the augmentation axiom; it need not be hereditary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((E,\mathcal F)\) is a greedoid exactly when \(\varnothing\in\mathcal F\), accessibility, and augmentation hold.

children.title: Exchange-Strength Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Structural boundaries among hereditary, exchange, and accessibility regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Exchange-Strength Hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical comparison of hereditary, accessible, and augmentation axioms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite set system \((E,\mathcal F)\), heredity implies accessibility. Consequently, every matroid independent-set system is both an independence system and a greedoid. Neither converse holds in general: a greedoid may fail heredity, while an independence system may fail augmentation. Thus the matroid axioms combine the hereditary strength of independence systems with the augmentation property shared by greedoids, but independence systems and greedoids are not nested classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every matroid is both an independence system and a greedoid, while general independence systems and greedoids are incomparable.
assumptions_latex: All classes are interpreted through their standard feasible-set axioms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\text{matroids}\}\subseteq\{\text{independence systems}\}\cap\{\text{greedoids}\}\), with neither ambient class contained in the other.

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Cryptomorphic Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of finite matroid independent-set, basis, circuit, and rank descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite ground set \(E\), a matroid may equivalently be specified by any one of its independent sets \(\mathcal I\), bases \(\mathcal B\), circuits \(\mathcal C\), or rank function \(r:2^E\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), provided the corresponding standard axioms hold. The translations are \[\mathcal B=\max_{\subseteq}\mathcal I,\qquad \mathcal C=\min_{\subseteq}(2^E\setminus\mathcal I),\qquad r(X)=\max\{|I|:I\subseteq X,\ I\in\mathcal I\},\] and \[\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq E:r(I)=|I|\}.\] Hence each representation determines the others uniquely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent sets, bases, circuits, and rank functions satisfying their matroid axioms determine the same finite matroid and uniquely recover one another.
assumptions_latex: The selected representation satisfies its standard matroid axioms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The representations \(\mathcal I\), \(\mathcal B\), \(\mathcal C\), and \(r\) determine one another uniquely.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid Characteristic Polynomial and Whitney Numbers of the First Kind
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to a finite matroid so that the subset sum and coefficient sequence are finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite matroid $M$ with ground set $E$, its characteristic (or chromatic) polynomial is
\[p(M;z)=\sum_{X\subseteq E}(-1)^{|X|}z^{r(M)-r(X)}.\]
The Whitney numbers of the first kind are the coefficients $w_0,\ldots,w_{r(M)}$ determined by
\[p(M;z)=\sum_{k=0}^{r(M)}w_k z^{r(M)-k}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The characteristic, or chromatic, polynomial of a finite matroid is the alternating subset sum whose exponent is the difference between the rank of the matroid and the rank of the subset. Its coefficients, indexed by rank, are the Whitney numbers of the first kind.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a finite matroid with ground set }E
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(M;z)=\sum_{X\subseteq E}(-1)^{|X|}z^{r(M)-r(X)}=\sum_{k=0}^{r(M)}w_k z^{r(M)-k},\quad w_k\text{ are the Whitney numbers of the first kind}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of the cycle matroid and characterization of its independent sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph \(G\), the cycle matroid, or polygon matroid, \(M(G)\) has ground set \(E(G)\) and circuits equal to the edge sets of cycles of \(G\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Construction of a Matroid from Circuit Axioms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Circuit-axiom construction of a matroid through its independent sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a set and let \(\mathcal C\subseteq 2^E\) satisfy (C1) \(\varnothing\notin\mathcal C\), (C2) \(C_1,C_2\in\mathcal C\) and \(C_1\subseteq C_2\) imply \(C_1=C_2\), and (C3) if distinct \(C_1,C_2\in\mathcal C\) and \(e\in C_1\cap C_2\), then some \(C_3\in\mathcal C\) satisfies \(C_3\subseteq (C_1\cup C_2)\setminus\{e\}\). Define \(\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq E:\nexists C\in\mathcal C\text{ with }C\subseteq I\}\). Then \((E,\mathcal I)\) is a matroid whose circuit collection is \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family that excludes the empty set, is an inclusion antichain, and satisfies circuit elimination determines a matroid: the subsets containing no member of the family are its independent sets, and the given family is exactly its circuit family.
assumptions_latex: \(C_1\ne C_2,\ e\in C_1\cap C_2\Rightarrow \exists C_3\in\mathcal C:\ C_3\subseteq(C_1\cup C_2)\setminus\{e\}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((E,\mathcal I)\text{ is a matroid and }\mathcal C(M)=\mathcal C\), where \(\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq E:\nexists C\in\mathcal C,\ C\subseteq I\}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Isomorphism defined through preservation and reflection of independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Matroids \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) are isomorphic, written \(M_1\cong M_2\), if there exists a bijection \(\psi:E(M_1)\to E(M_2)\) such that, for every \(X\subseteq E(M_1)\), \(X\) is independent in \(M_1\) if and only if \(\psi(X)\) is independent in \(M_2\). Such a bijection \(\psi\) is an isomorphism from \(M_1\) to \(M_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two matroids are isomorphic when a bijection between their ground sets preserves and reflects independence for every subset; the bijection is called a matroid isomorphism.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_1\cong M_2\iff \forall X\subseteq E(M_1),\ [X\in\mathcal I(M_1)\iff\psi(X)\in\mathcal I(M_2)].\)

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite matroid duality through complementary bases and rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid with basis family \(\mathcal B(M)\) and rank function \(r_M\). Its dual \(M^*\) is the matroid on \(E\) whose bases are \[\mathcal B(M^*)=\{E\setminus B:B\in\mathcal B(M)\}.\] For every \(X\subseteq E\), its rank is \[r_{M^*}(X)=|X|-r_M(E)+r_M(E\setminus X).\] Duality is involutive: \((M^*)^*=M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual matroid has complements of the original bases as bases; its rank follows the complementary-rank formula, and dualizing twice recovers the matroid.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a matroid on a finite ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B(M^*)=\{E\setminus B:B\in\mathcal B(M)\}\) and \((M^*)^*=M\).

notation.meaning: rank function of the original matroid

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extract contains two related definitions; the repeated reference to $C_2^*$ is interpreted from the displayed condition as separation of $C_2^*$ from $C_3^*$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $C_1^*,C_2^*,C_3^*$ be distinct cocircuits of a matroid $M$. The cocircuit $C_1^*$ separates $C_2^*$ from $C_3^*$ if no component of $M\setminus C_1^*$ contains $(C_2^*\cup C_3^*)-C_1^*$; equivalently, no bridge of $M\setminus C_1^*$ contains that set. The ordered collection $(C_1^*,C_2^*,C_3^*)$ is a Fournier triple if $C_1^*\cap C_2^*\cap C_3^*\ne\varnothing$ and none of the three cocircuits separates the other two.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One cocircuit separates two others when, after deleting it, no component—or equivalently no bridge—contains all remaining elements of the other two. Three distinct cocircuits form a Fournier triple when they share an element and none separates the other two.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_1^*\text{ separates }C_2^*\text{ from }C_3^*\iff\nexists\text{ a component of }M\setminus C_1^*\text{ containing }(C_2^*\cup C_3^*)-C_1^*;\quad (C_1^*,C_2^*,C_3^*)\text{ is a Fournier triple}\iff C_1^*\cap C_2^*\cap C_3^*\ne\varnothing\text{ and none separates the other two.}

knowledge_statements.title: Deletion Minors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion of an arbitrary subset from a finite matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid and let \(D\subseteq E\). The deletion \(M\setminus D\) is the matroid on \(E\setminus D\) with independent sets \[\mathcal I(M\setminus D)=\{I\in\mathcal I:I\subseteq E\setminus D\}.\] Equivalently, for every \(X\subseteq E\setminus D\), its rank satisfies \[r_{M\setminus D}(X)=r_M(X).\] Any matroid obtained by a sequence of deletions is a deletion minor of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting elements restricts a matroid to the remaining ground set; independence and rank of remaining subsets are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\setminus D\) is the restriction of \(M\) to \(E\setminus D\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Common-Independent-Set Characterization of a Prescribed Matroid k-Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when two prescribed disjoint subsets can lie on opposite sides of a k-separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M$ be a matroid, let $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, and let $X_1,X_2\subseteq E(M)$ be disjoint with $|X_1|,|X_2|\ge k$. Define $t=r(M)+k-r_M(X_1)-r_M(X_2)$. Then $M$ has a $k$-separation $(Y_1,Y_2)$ satisfying $X_1\subseteq Y_1$ and $X_2\subseteq Y_2$ if and only if the matroids $M/X_1\setminus X_2$ and $M/X_2\setminus X_1$ have no common independent set of cardinality $t$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a matroid M, a positive integer k, and disjoint subsets X1 and X2 of at least k elements each, set t equal to the rank of M plus k minus the ranks of X1 and X2. There is a k-separation placing X1 and X2 on opposite prescribed sides exactly when the two corresponding contraction-deletion minors have no common independent set of size t.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\exists\text{ a }k\text{-separation }(Y_1,Y_2):X_1\subseteq Y_1,\ X_2\subseteq Y_2\bigr]\iff\bigl[M/X_1\setminus X_2\text{ and }M/X_2\setminus X_1\text{ have no common independent set of size }t\bigr].

knowledge_statements.title: Contraction Minors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contraction of an arbitrary subset from a finite matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\), and let \(C\subseteq E\). The contraction \(M/C\) is the matroid on \(E\setminus C\) whose rank function is \[r_{M/C}(X)=r_M(X\cup C)-r_M(C)\qquad\text{for every }X\subseteq E\setminus C.\] Equivalently, \(M/C=(M^*\setminus C)^*\). Any matroid obtained by a sequence of contractions is a contraction minor of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contracting a subset removes it after accounting for its rank; contraction is equivalently dual to deletion in the dual matroid.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a matroid on a finite ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{M/C}(X)=r_M(X\cup C)-r_M(C)\) for all \(X\subseteq E\setminus C\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard rank-function definition of matroid contraction
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The contraction rank formula and deletion–duality identity are precise and appropriately scoped, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines general matroid minors and their deletion–contraction normal form, with disjoint operation sets understood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid. Every finite sequence of deletions and contractions from \(M\) can be written as \(M\setminus X/Y=M/Y\setminus X\) for disjoint sets \(X,Y\subseteq E(M)\), either of which may be empty. A matroid of this form is a minor of \(M\); it is a proper minor when \(X\cup Y\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minor of M is any matroid obtained by a sequence of deletions and contractions. Equivalently, it has the form M minus X contracted by Y, or M contracted by Y minus X, where X and Y are disjoint and may be empty. It is proper when at least one element is deleted or contracted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N\text{ is a minor of }M\iff N=M\setminus X/Y=M/Y\setminus X\text{ for some disjoint }X,Y\subseteq E(M);\quad N\text{ is proper}\iff X\cup Y\ne\varnothing

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reconstruction from Single-Element Deletion and Contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when two matroids with the same deletion and contraction at an element can differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be matroids on the same ground set $E$, and let $e\in E$. Then $$M_1\setminus e=M_2\setminus e\ \text{ and }\ M_1/e=M_2/e$$ if and only if either $M_1=M_2$, or $e$ is a loop of one of $M_1,M_2$ and a coloop of the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two matroids on the same ground set have identical deletion and contraction at e exactly when they are equal, except that they may differ by making e a loop in one matroid and a coloop in the other.

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Sums
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct sums of finitely many matroids on disjoint ground sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_i=(E_i,\mathcal I_i)\) for \(i=1,\ldots,k\) be finite matroids with pairwise disjoint ground sets. Their direct sum \(M=\bigoplus_{i=1}^k M_i\) is the matroid on \(E=\bigcup_{i=1}^k E_i\) whose independent sets satisfy \[\mathcal I(M)=\{I\subseteq E:I\cap E_i\in\mathcal I_i\text{ for every }i\}.\] Its rank is additive across components: \[r_M(X)=\sum_{i=1}^k r_{M_i}(X\cap E_i)\qquad\text{for every }X\subseteq E.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct sum combines matroids on disjoint ground sets; independence is componentwise and rank is the sum of component ranks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\) is independent in \(\bigoplus_i M_i\) exactly when every \(I\cap E_i\) is independent in \(M_i\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a labelled-tree representation and the permitted intersections between the ground sets of its vertex labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid-labelled tree is a tree \(T\) with vertex set \(\{M_1,\ldots,M_k\}\) for some \(k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) such that: (i) every \(M_i\) is a matroid; (ii) if \(M_{j_1}\) and \(M_{j_2}\) are joined by an edge \(e_i\), then \(E(M_{j_1})\cap E(M_{j_2})=\{e_i\}\), and \(\{e_i\}\) is not a separator of either \(M_{j_1}\) or \(M_{j_2}\); and (iii) if \(M_{j_1}\) and \(M_{j_2}\) are nonadjacent, then \(E(M_{j_1})\cap E(M_{j_2})=\varnothing\). The matroids \(M_1,\ldots,M_k\) are called the vertex labels of \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid-labelled tree is a tree whose vertices are matroids. Adjacent labels intersect exactly in the element naming their edge, that singleton is not a separator of either label, and nonadjacent labels have disjoint ground sets. The matroids are called the vertex labels.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is a tree with vertex set }\{M_1,\ldots,M_k\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bases of series and parallel connections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded basis characterization with its loop and coloop boundary assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E(M_1)\cap E(M_2)=\{p\}\), \(E=E(M_1)\cup E(M_2)\), and \(B\subseteq E\). (i) If \(M_1,M_2\) do not both have \(p\) as a coloop, then \(B\) is a basis of \(S(M_1,M_2)\) iff there are disjoint bases \(B_i\) of \(M_i\) with \(B=B_1\cup B_2\). (ii) If \(M_1,M_2\) do not both have \(p\) as a loop, then \(B\) is a basis of \(P(M_1,M_2)\) iff there are bases \(B_i\) of \(M_i\) such that either \(p\in B_1\cap B_2\) and \(B=B_1\cup B_2\), or \(p\) belongs to exactly one of \(B_1,B_2\) and \(B=(B_1\cup B_2)-p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For matroids meeting only at p, a series-connection basis is exactly the union of disjoint component bases, provided p is not a coloop of both components. A parallel-connection basis comes from component bases that either both contain p, retaining it in their union, or exactly one contains p, deleting it from the union; this characterization assumes p is not a loop of both components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}B\in\mathcal B(S(M_1,M_2))&\iff \exists B_i\in\mathcal B(M_i): B_1\cap B_2=\varnothing,\ B=B_1\cup B_2,\\ B\in\mathcal B(P(M_1,M_2))&\iff \exists B_i\in\mathcal B(M_i)\text{ satisfying alternatives (a) or (b),}\end{aligned}\text{ under the respective stated boundary assumptions.}

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between nontrivial matroid sum decompositions and higher connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid on ground set \(E\). A partition \((X,E\setminus X)\), with \(|X|,|E\setminus X|\ge k\), is a \(k\)-separation when \[r_M(X)+r_M(E\setminus X)-r_M(E)\le k-1.\] A nontrivial direct-sum decomposition exists exactly when a \(1\)-separation exists. Consequently, connected matroids are precisely those having no nontrivial direct-sum decomposition. More generally, the absence of \(1\)- and \(2\)-separations marks the boundary beyond which decomposition by \(1\)- and \(2\)-sums is unavailable; such matroids are \(3\)-connected, subject to the usual minimum-size convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separations identify matroid decomposition boundaries: connected matroids admit no nontrivial direct sum, while 3-connected matroids admit neither 1- nor 2-separations.
assumptions_latex: The connectivity convention requires both sides of a \(k\)-separation to have at least \(k\) elements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is connected exactly when it has no nontrivial direct-sum decomposition; absence of \(1\)- and \(2\)-separations is the corresponding \(3\)-connectivity boundary.

notation.meaning: A partition of the ground set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Signed graphs, switching equivalence, and signed minors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collects the independent definitions and equivalences in the extract without proof.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A signed graph is $G=(V,E,\Sigma)$, where $(V,E)$ is undirected and $\Sigma\subseteq E$; an edge set, path, or circuit is odd when it contains an odd number of edges of $\Sigma$. Two signings $\Sigma,\Sigma'$ have the same odd circuits iff $\Sigma\triangle\Sigma'$ is a cut, in which case they are equivalent. The inclusionwise minimal odd-circuit covers are exactly the inclusionwise minimal signings equivalent to $\Sigma$, and hence $B\triangle\Sigma$ is a cut for every inclusionwise minimal odd-circuit cover $B$. Signed-graph deletion is inherited from the underlying graph; contraction first switches an incident vertex when the contracted edge is signed, so its outcome is unique up to signing equivalence. A signed minor is obtained by deletions, contractions, and replacement by an equivalent signing. Writing $\operatorname{odd}\text{-}K_n=(V(K_n),E(K_n),E(K_n))$, a signed graph contains an odd $K_4$-subdivision iff it has $\operatorname{odd}\text{-}K_4$ as a minor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A signed graph is an undirected graph with a distinguished edge set, and parity is measured by the number of distinguished edges used. Two signings determine the same odd circuits exactly when their symmetric difference is a cut. Minimal odd-circuit covers are precisely minimal equivalent signings. Signed minors use deletion, switching-compatible contraction, and equivalent resigning. An odd K4 subdivision exists exactly when odd-K4 is a signed minor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal C_{\mathrm{odd}}(\Sigma)=\mathcal C_{\mathrm{odd}}(\Sigma')\iff \Sigma\triangle\Sigma'\text{ is a cut},\qquad G\text{ contains an odd }K_4\text{-subdivision}\iff \operatorname{odd}\text{-}K_4\preceq G.

knowledge_statements.title: Graphic Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite undirected multigraph cycle-matroid definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite undirected multigraph \(G=(V,E)\), the graphic matroid, or cycle matroid, \(M(G)\) is the matroid on ground set \(E\) whose independent sets are exactly the edge sets containing no graph cycle. Thus \[\mathcal I(M(G))=\{F\subseteq E:(V,F)\text{ is a forest}\}.\] Its circuits are the edge sets of cycles, its bases are the spanning forests of \(G\), and its rank satisfies \[r_{M(G)}(F)=|V|-c(V,F),\] where isolated vertices are counted among the connected components of \((V,F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graphic matroid has graph edges as elements and forests as independent sets; its circuits are cycles and its bases are spanning forests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(G)=(E,\mathcal I(M(G)))\) is a matroid with rank \(r_{M(G)}(F)=|V|-c(V,F)\).

notation.meaning: Number of connected components of the spanning subgraph \((V,F)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the antichain characterization for the minor order on finite graphs or matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quasi-order is a pair \((\mathcal X,\leq)\) in which \(\leq\) is reflexive and transitive. For a set \(\mathcal X\) of graphs or matroids, define \(Y\preccurlyeq Z\) when \(Y\) is isomorphic to a minor of \(Z\); then \((\mathcal X,\preccurlyeq)\) is the minor quasi-order. A quasi-order \((\mathcal X,\leq)\) is a well-quasi-order if every infinite sequence \(X_1,X_2,\ldots\) contains indices \(i<j\) with \(X_i\leq X_j\). For a set of finite graphs or a set of matroids under \(\preccurlyeq\), this holds if and only if the set contains no infinite antichain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasi-order is a reflexive, transitive relation. Minor containment up to isomorphism defines a quasi-order on graphs or matroids. It is a well-quasi-order when every infinite sequence has an earlier member below a later one; for finite graphs or matroids under the minor order, this is equivalent to having no infinite antichain.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is a set and \(\leq\) is a binary relation on \(\mathcal X\).
For the minor-order specialization, \(\mathcal X\) is a set of finite graphs or a set of matroids.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\mathcal X,\preccurlyeq)\text{ is well-quasi-ordered}\iff \mathcal X\text{ contains no infinite minor-order antichain.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A four-regime classification of element growth for simple members of a minor-closed class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) be a minor-closed class of matroids. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a paired-set exchange system and its associated family of subsets of \(U\cup W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\) and \(W\) be disjoint sets and let \(\Lambda\subseteq 2^U\times 2^W\). The triple \((U,W,\Lambda)\) is a bimatroid (linking system) if: (i) \((\varnothing,\varnothing)\in\Lambda\); (ii) for every \((X,Y)\in\Lambda\) and \(x\in X\), there exists \(y\in Y\) such that \((X-x,Y-y)\in\Lambda\); (iii) for every \((X,Y)\in\Lambda\) and \(y\in Y\), there exists \(x\in X\) such that \((X-x,Y-y)\in\Lambda\); and (iv) for all \((X_1,Y_1),(X_2,Y_2)\in\Lambda\), there exists \((X,Y)\in\Lambda\) with
\[
X_1\subseteq X\subseteq X_1\cup X_2,\qquad Y_2\subseteq Y\subseteq Y_1\cup Y_2.
\]
Axioms (ii) and (iii) imply \(|X|=|Y|\) for every \((X,Y)\in\Lambda\). The associated family is
\[
\mathcal B:=\{(U\setminus X)\cup Y\mid (X,Y)\in\Lambda\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bimatroid is a collection of equally sized paired subsets of two disjoint sets satisfying deletion and amalgamation axioms; each pair produces the set obtained by replacing X in U with Y.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (U,W,\Lambda)\text{ is a bimatroid exactly under axioms (i)--(iv), with }|X|=|Y|\text{ for }(X,Y)\in\Lambda\text{ and }\mathcal B=\{(U\setminus X)\cup Y:(X,Y)\in\Lambda\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Representable Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite matroids represented by matrix columns over a fixed field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid and \(\mathbb F\) a field. The matroid \(M\) is representable over \(\mathbb F\) if there exist a matrix \(A\) over \(\mathbb F\) and a bijection from \(E\) to the columns of \(A\) such that, for every \(X\subseteq E\), \[X\in\mathcal I\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{the columns of \(A\) indexed by \(X\) are linearly independent over \(\mathbb F\)}.\] Equivalently, its rank function obeys \(r_M(X)=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F}(A_X)\) for every \(X\subseteq E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is representable over a field when its independent sets are exactly the linearly independent column subsets of a matrix over that field.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is \(\mathbb F\)-representable exactly when \(r_M(X)=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F}(A_X)\) for some matrix \(A\) and every \(X\subseteq E\).

notation.meaning: Submatrix consisting of columns indexed by \(X\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation and structural properties of P_8^{=}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded profile; the parameter restrictions apply only to the displayed matrix representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the displayed-matrix conditions, the matrix represents P_8^{=} over \mathbb F. The matroid P_8^{=} is obtained from P_8 by relaxing its only pair of disjoint circuit-hyperplanes. It is \mathbb F-representable if and only if |\mathbb F|\ge 5 and is an excluded minor for GF(4)-representability. It is neither graphic, cographic, regular, near-regular, transversal, nor a strict gammoid. It is self-dual but not identically self-dual, and its automorphism group is transitive on points and on hyperplanes. It is not a tipless 4-spike; every single-element contraction has the stated relaxed-P_7 isomorphism type. It is algebraic over every field.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With the stated parameter restrictions, the displayed matrix represents P_8^=. The matroid is obtained from P_8 by the stated relaxation, is representable precisely over fields of size at least five, is an excluded minor for GF(4)-representability, and has the listed class, duality, symmetry, contraction, and algebraicity properties.
assumptions_latex: \text{For the displayed matrix clause, }\mathbb F\text{ is a field}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_8^{=}\text{ has the stated representation, relaxation, class-membership, duality, symmetry, contraction, and algebraicity properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A permutation \sigma of V(r,\mathbb F) is a nonsingular semilinear transformation if there exist a nonsingular linear transformation \tau of V(r,\mathbb F) and an automorphism \alpha of \mathbb F such that, whenever \tau(v)=(w_1,\ldots,w_r), one has \sigma(v)=(\alpha(w_1),\ldots,\alpha(w_r)) for every v\in V(r,\mathbb F).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representability, class, duality, relaxation, and roundedness properties of $Q_6$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid $Q_6$ is $\mathbb F$-representable if and only if $|\mathbb F|\ge 4$. It is not graphic, cographic, regular, or near-regular, but it is transversal, a strict gammoid, a gammoid, self-dual but not identically self-dual, and algebraic over every field. Its automorphism group is non-transitive, and it is the unique relaxation of $\mathcal W^3$. If $N$ is a matroid with at least four elements, then $\{N\}$ is 1-rounded if and only if $N\cong U_{2,4}$, $N\cong M(\mathcal W_2)$, or $N\cong Q_6$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Q6 has the stated representability, class, duality, automorphism, algebraicity, and unique-relaxation properties. Among matroids with at least four elements, it is one of exactly three isomorphism types whose singleton class is 1-rounded.
assumptions_latex: N\text{ is a matroid with }|E(N)|\ge4\text{ for the 1-rounded classification.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-field bounds on inequivalent matroid representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collects five uniqueness or multiplicity bounds with their exact field, connectivity, and excluded-minor hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The following hold: (i) every ternary matroid is uniquely $GF(3)$-representable; (ii) if $q$ is a prime power with $q\notin\{2,3\}$, then every $3$-connected matroid having neither a $U_{2,5}$-minor nor a $U_{3,5}$-minor has at most $q-2$ inequivalent $GF(q)$-representations; (iii) if $q$ is a prime power with $q\notin\{2,3\}$, then every $3$-connected ternary matroid has at most $q-2$ inequivalent $GF(q)$-representations; (iv) every $3$-connected quaternary matroid is uniquely $GF(4)$-representable; and (v) every $3$-connected $GF(5)$-representable matroid has at most six inequivalent $GF(5)$-representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ternary matroids are uniquely representable over GF(3). For prime powers q other than 2 and 3, a 3-connected matroid excluding U(2,5) and U(3,5), and a 3-connected ternary matroid, have at most q−2 inequivalent GF(q) representations. Three-connected quaternary matroids are uniquely representable over GF(4), while three-connected GF(5)-representable matroids have at most six inequivalent GF(5) representations.
assumptions_latex: q\text{ is a prime power with }q\notin\{2,3\}\text{ in parts (ii) and (iii)}
M\text{ has no }U_{2,5}\text{- or }U_{3,5}\text{-minor in part (ii)}
M\text{ is ternary in parts (i) and (iii), quaternary in part (iv), and }GF(5)\text{-representable in part (v)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_{GF(3)}(M)=1\text{ in (i)},\quad r_{GF(q)}(M)\le q-2\text{ in (ii),(iii)},\quad r_{GF(4)}(M)=1\text{ in (iv)},\quad r_{GF(5)}(M)\le6\text{ in (v)},\text{ where }r_K(M)\text{ counts inequivalent }K\text{-representations.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Properties and theorem roles of U_{3,6}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded profile of the rank-three uniform matroid on six elements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: U_{3,6} consists of six points freely placed in the plane and is the tipless free 3-spike. It is \mathbb F-representable if and only if |\mathbb F|\ge4. It is neither graphic, cographic, regular, nor near-regular, but is transversal, a strict gammoid, and a gammoid. It is identically self-dual, its automorphism group is the symmetric group, and it is the unique relaxation of P_6. Every 3-connected matroid M with r(M),r^*(M)>2 has a minor isomorphic to one of M(K_4),\mathcal W^3,Q_6,P_6,U_{3,6}; if M is also non-binary, the list is \mathcal W^3,P_6,Q_6,U_{3,6}. If M is 3-connected and GF(q)-representable with no U_{3,6}-minor, then M has at most (q-2)! inequivalent GF(q)-representations. The matroid U_{3,6} is algebraic over every field.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: U_{3,6} is six freely placed planar points and the tipless free 3-spike. It has the stated representation, class, duality, symmetry, relaxation, unavoidable-minor, representation-bound, and algebraicity properties.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb F\text{ is a field for the field-representability assertion}
M\text{ is 3-connected and }r(M),r^*(M)>2\text{ for the unavoidable-minor assertions}
M\text{ is non-binary for the second unavoidable-minor assertion}
M\text{ is 3-connected, GF}(q)\text{-representable, and has no }U_{3,6}\text{-minor for the representation bound}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_{3,6}\text{ has the stated properties, and under the final hypotheses }M\text{ has at most }(q-2)!\text{ inequivalent GF}(q)\text{-representations.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semilinear characterization of equivalent matroid representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes full representation equivalence using a common semilinear transformation and individual column scalings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M be a matroid on E=\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}, let r\ge 1, and let A_1,A_2\in\mathbb F^{r\times n}. Suppose that for i\in\{1,2\}, the map e_j\mapsto v_j^{(i)}, where v_j^{(i)} is column j of A_i, is an isomorphism M\cong M[A_i]. Then A_1 and A_2 are equivalent representations of M if and only if there exist a nonsingular semilinear transformation \sigma of V(r,\mathbb F) and nonzero c_1,\ldots,c_n\in\mathbb F such that v_j^{(2)}=c_j\sigma(v_j^{(1)}) for every j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two labeled matrices representing the same positive-rank matroid are equivalent exactly when a common nonsingular semilinear transformation followed by an independent nonzero scaling of each column maps the first representation to the second.
assumptions_latex: e_j\mapsto v_j^{(i)}\text{ is an isomorphism }M\cong M[A_i]\quad(i=1,2)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_1\sim A_2\iff \exists\sigma\text{ nonsingular semilinear},\ \exists c_1,\ldots,c_n\in\mathbb F^{\times}:\ v_j^{(2)}=c_j\sigma(v_j^{(1)})\ \forall j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient criterion for representability of a matroid over an arbitrary field, expressed through a jointly chosen family of hyperplane-indexed functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid and \(\mathbb F\) a field. Then \(M\) is \(\mathbb F\)-representable if and only if there exists a family \((f_H)_{H\in\mathcal H(M)}\), with \(f_H:E(M)\to\mathbb F\), such that: (i) for every hyperplane \(H\), \(H=\{x\in E(M):f_H(x)=0\}\); and (ii) whenever \(H_1,H_2,H_3\) are distinct hyperplanes with \(r(H_1\cap H_2\cap H_3)=r(M)-2\), there exist \(c_1,c_2,c_3\in\mathbb F\setminus\{0\}\) such that \(c_1f_{H_1}+c_2f_{H_2}+c_3f_{H_3}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is representable over a field exactly when one can jointly choose a field-valued function for every hyperplane so that each hyperplane is its function's zero set and the functions for any three distinct hyperplanes whose common intersection has rank two below the matroid rank satisfy a linear dependence with all three coefficients nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is }\mathbb F\text{-representable}\iff \exists (f_H)_{H\in\mathcal H(M)}\text{ satisfying conditions (i) and (ii)}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let q be a prime power. For r\ge 1, AG(r-1,q) is the rank-r affine geometry over GF(q), has q^{r-1} elements, and is obtained by deleting a hyperplane from PG(r-1,q). The low-rank cases satisfy AG(-1,q)\cong U_{0,0}, AG(0,q)\cong U_{1,1}, AG(1,q)\cong U_{2,q}, and AG(2,2)\cong U_{3,4}. If r=3 and q\ge 4, or if r\ge 4, then AG(r-1,q) is \mathbb F-representable if and only if \mathbb F contains GF(q) as a subfield. For r,q\ge 3, it is neither graphic, cographic, regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, nor a gammoid. For r\ge 3, it is identically self-dual if and only if (r-1,q)=(3,2), and otherwise it is not self-dual. Its automorphism group is symmetric when r\le 2 or (r-1,q)=(2,2), and doubly transitive otherwise. Every restriction to a flat is AG(k-1,q) for some k\le r, and the simplification of every proper contraction is PG(k-1,q) for some k<r. It is 3-connected unless (r-1,q)\in\{(1,2),(2,2)\}. If r=3 and q\ge 5, or if r\ge 4, it is algebraic over \mathbb F if and only if \operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)=\operatorname{char}(GF(q)).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AG(r−1,q) is obtained by deleting a hyperplane from PG(r−1,q) and, for positive rank, has q^(r−1) elements. The stated low-rank cases, field-representation ranges, class exclusions, self-duality exception, automorphism regimes, flat restrictions, simplified contractions, connectivity exceptions, and characteristic-dependent algebraicity all depend on the parameter conditions given in the extract.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: AG(r-1,q)\text{ has the stated construction, size, representation, class, duality, symmetry, minor, connectivity, and algebraicity properties in their specified parameter ranges.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Critical exponent of a GF(q)-representable matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the loop boundary, simplification invariance, and coordinatization-independent characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a rank-\(r\) matroid representable over \(\mathrm{GF}(q)\). If \(M\) is loopless and \(\psi:E(M)\to V(r,q)\) is a coordinatization, its critical exponent \(c(M;q)\) is the least \(j\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) for which there exist hyperplanes \(H_1,\ldots,H_j\) of \(V(r,q)\) satisfying \(\bigl(\bigcap_{i=1}^jH_i\bigr)\cap\psi(E(M))=\varnothing\). If \(M\) has a loop, set \(c(M;q)=\infty\). For loopless \(M\), \(c(M;q)=c(\operatorname{si}(M);q)\), and this invariant is independent of \(\psi\), with \[c(M;q)=\min\{j\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}:p(M;q^j)>0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a loopless rank-r matroid represented over GF(q), the critical exponent is the smallest nonnegative number of hyperplanes whose intersection avoids every representing vector. It is infinite when the matroid has a loop, is unchanged by simplification, is independent of the coordinatization, and equals the least j for which p(M;q^j) is positive.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a rank-}r\text{ matroid representable over }\mathrm{GF}(q)
\psi:E(M)\to V(r,q)\text{ is a }\mathrm{GF}(q)\text{-coordinatization when }M\text{ is loopless}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c(M;q)=\min\{j\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}:p(M;q^j)>0\}\text{ for loopless }M,\quad c(M;q)=\infty\text{ if }M\text{ has a loop}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Profile of the projective-geometry matroid PG(r−1,q)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-r projective geometries over GF(q), including the stated low-rank conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let q be a prime power. The rank-r projective geometry PG(r-1,q) is the simple matroid associated with V(r,q) and has (q^r-1)/(q-1) elements. Moreover, PG(-1,q)\cong U_{0,0}, PG(0,q)\cong U_{1,1}, and PG(1,q)\cong U_{2,q+1}. For r\ge 3, it is \mathbb F-representable if and only if \mathbb F contains GF(q) as a subfield; it is neither graphic, cographic, regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, nor a gammoid, and it is not self-dual. Its automorphism group is symmetric for r\le 2 and doubly transitive for r\ge 3. Every simple GF(q)-representable matroid of rank at most r is a restriction of PG(r-1,q). Every restriction to a flat is isomorphic to PG(k-1,q) for some k\le r, and the simplification of every proper contraction is isomorphic to PG(k-1,q) for some k<r. For r\ge 3, PG(r-1,q) is algebraic over \mathbb F if and only if \operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)=\operatorname{char}(GF(q)).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PG(r−1,q) is the rank-r simple matroid associated with the r-dimensional vector space over GF(q), and it has (q^r−1)/(q−1) elements. The extract gives its low-rank uniform-matroid cases. At rank at least three it is representable over a field exactly when that field contains GF(q), and it is not graphic, cographic, regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, a gammoid, or self-dual. It is universal for simple GF(q)-representable matroids of rank at most r under restriction. Its flat restrictions and simplified proper contractions are lower-rank projective geometries, and its algebraicity is characterized by equality of field characteristics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: PG(r-1,q)\text{ has the stated size, representation, class-exclusion, symmetry, universality, minor, and algebraicity properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Canonical Representations and Transversal Circuits of Spikes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provides projective normal forms for represented spikes and tipless spikes, together with a circuit criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $r\ge3$, let $\mathbb F$ be a field, and let $M$ be an $\mathbb F$-representable rank-$r$ spike with legs $\{t,x_i,y_i\}$ such that $\{x_1,\ldots,x_r\}$ is independent. Every $\mathbb F$-representation of $M$ is projectively equivalent to $[I_r\mid A_r\mid\mathbf 1]$, with columns ordered $x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_r,t$. For every $K\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$, the set $\{x_k:k\notin K\}\cup\{y_k:k\in K\}$ is a circuit if and only if $\sum_{k\in K}\alpha_k=-1$. If additionally $r\ge4$ and $N$ is an $\mathbb F$-representable rank-$r$ tipless spike with legs $\{x_i,y_i\}$ and independent $\{x_1,\ldots,x_r\}$, then every representation of $N$ is projectively equivalent to $[I_r\mid A_r]$ with columns ordered $x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_r$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A represented rank-r spike with an independent choice of one element from each leg has the stated projective normal form. Its corresponding transversal is a circuit exactly when the selected parameters sum to −1. For rank at least four, the analogous tipless spike has the normal form obtained by omitting the tip column.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is an }\mathbb F\text{-representable rank-}r\text{ spike with legs }\{t,x_i,y_i\}
\text{For the final assertion: }r\ge4\text{ and }N\text{ is an }\mathbb F\text{-representable rank-}r\text{ tipless spike with independent }\{x_1,\ldots,x_r\}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quaternary-obstruction, representability, class, relaxation, and exchange properties of $P_6$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The excluded minors for quaternary matroids are $U_{2,6},U_{4,6},P_6,F_7^-,(F_7^-)^*,P_8,$ and $P_8^=$. The matroid $P_6$ is $\mathbb F$-representable if and only if $|\mathbb F|\ge 5$. It is not graphic, cographic, regular, or near-regular, but it is transversal, a strict gammoid, a gammoid, self-dual but not identically self-dual, and algebraic over every field. Its automorphism group is non-transitive. It is the unique relaxation of $Q_6$, is obtained from $U_{2,6}$ by a $\Delta$-$Y$ exchange, and is obtained from $U_{4,6}$ by a $Y$-$\Delta$ exchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: P6 is one of the seven excluded minors for quaternary matroids and has the stated representability, class, duality, automorphism, algebraicity, unique-relaxation, and exchange properties.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_6\text{ has the stated quaternary-obstruction, representability, class, unique-relaxation, and exchange properties.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definition and structural properties of the free swirl $\Psi_r$ and jointed free swirl $\Psi_r^+$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For $r\ge3$, the rank-$r$ free swirl $\Psi_r$ has ground set $\{a_1,b_1,\ldots,a_r,b_r\}$ and the cyclic family of non-spanning circuits specified in the extract; $\Psi_3\cong U_{3,6}$. The jointed free swirl $\Psi_r^+$ is obtained by freely adding an element on each $3$-point line of the rank-$r$ whirl, and deleting all whirl spokes from $\Psi_r^+$ yields $\Psi_r$. The free swirl $\Psi_r$ is neither binary nor ternary. The matroid $\Psi_3$ is $\mathbb F$-representable if and only if $|\mathbb F|\ge4$, while $\Psi_3^+$ is representable if and only if $|\mathbb F|\ge5$. For $r\ge4$, $\Psi_r$ and $\Psi_r^+$ are representable over exactly the same fields. They are representable over every infinite field and over $GF(q)$ for $q\ge4$, except that when $q=2^p$ and $2^p-1$ is prime, they are non-representable for all sufficiently large $r$. Each $\Psi_r$ is transversal, a strict gammoid, a gammoid, identically self-dual, and $3$-connected; for $r\ge4$ it is not $4$-connected. It is neither graphic, cographic, regular, nor near-regular; each pair $a_i,b_i$ consists of clones; and it is algebraic over every field.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For r at least 3, Psi(r) is the rank-r free swirl with the specified cyclic non-spanning circuits, and Psi(3) is U(3,6). The jointed version arises from a whirl by free additions. The extract gives exact small-r field-size thresholds and a general finite-field exception. Free swirls are transversal gammoids, identically self-dual, 3-connected but generally not 4-connected, non-graphic and non-regular, and each designated pair consists of clones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Psi_r\text{ and }\Psi_r^+\text{ have the stated circuit structure and representability regimes, while }\Psi_r\text{ has the stated duality, connectivity, class-membership, and clone properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Single-automorphism normal form for equivalent representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalizes the field-automorphism component of an equivalence between positive-rank matroid representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathbb F be a field, and let A_1,A_2 be equivalent \mathbb F-representations of a matroid of positive rank. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded composite profile of the Pappus matroid.

Its automorphism group is transitive, it can be obtained from AG(2,3) by relaxing three disjoint three-point lines, and it is algebraic over every field.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_P\text{ has the stated field-representability, excluded-minor, class-exclusion, symmetry, relaxation, and algebraicity properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Absence of totally free minors implies unique representability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The second clause is retained literally as extracted. Because its representation count remains that of M rather than the varying minor, it yields only a tautological bound and must not be interpreted as a substantive minor-based multiplicity bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let q be a prime power and let M be a 3-connected \mathrm{GF}(q)-representable matroid. If M has no totally free minor, then M is uniquely \mathrm{GF}(q)-representable. Otherwise, writing r_q(M) for the number of inequivalent \mathrm{GF}(q)-representations of M, the extracted statement asserts r_q(M)\leq \max\{r_q(M):N\text{ is a totally free minor of }M\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a prime power q, a 3-connected GF(q)-representable matroid with no totally free minor is uniquely GF(q)-representable. Otherwise, the extract literally bounds the number of representations of M by a maximum of that same number indexed by the totally free minors of M; this clause is tautological as written.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(M\text{ has no totally free minor}\bigr)\Rightarrow\bigl(M\text{ is uniquely }\mathrm{GF}(q)\text{-representable}\bigr);\quad\text{otherwise }r_q(M)\leq\max_{N\text{ a totally free minor of }M}r_q(M).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent, projectively equivalent, and unique field representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for matrix representations of a fixed matroid over a field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A_1,A_2 be matrices over a field \mathbb F with M[A_1]=M[A_2]=M. They are equivalent representations of M if A_2 is obtainable from A_1 by a sequence of row or column swaps, row or column scalings, replacement of a row by its sum with another row, addition or removal of a zero row, or entrywise application of an automorphism of \mathbb F. They are projectively equivalent if the field-automorphism operation is never used. The matroid M is uniquely \mathbb F\text{-representable} if all its \mathbb F\text{-representations are equivalent}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two matrices over a field representing the same matroid are equivalent when one can be obtained from the other by the listed row and column operations, insertion or removal of zero rows, and entrywise field automorphisms. They are projectively equivalent when field automorphisms are excluded. A matroid is uniquely representable over the field when all its representations over that field are equivalent.
assumptions_latex: A_1,A_2\text{ are matrices over a field }\mathbb F
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Equivalence, projective equivalence, and unique }\mathbb F\text{-representability are defined as stated.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fundamental Graph Associated with a Basis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the bipartite graph encoded by the basis-fundamental-circuit incidence matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D^{\#} have rows indexed by B=\{e_1,\ldots,e_r\} and columns indexed by E\setminus B=\{e_{r+1},\ldots,e_n\}. The associated graph G(D^{\#}) is the simple bipartite graph with vertex classes B and E\setminus B in which e_i\in B and e_j\in E\setminus B are adjacent if and only if (D^{\#})_{e_i,e_j}=1. knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_i e_j\in E(G_B(M))\iff (D^{\#})_{e_i,e_j}=1\iff e_i\in C(e_j,B)\setminus\{e_j\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A stabilizing minor bounds representation multiplicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers a representation-count bound from a stabilizer to 3-connected representable matroids containing it as a minor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mathbb F$ be a field, and let $N$ be an $\mathbb F$-stabilizer for the class $\mathcal M$ of $\mathbb F$-representable matroids. If $N$ has $k$ inequivalent $\mathbb F$-representations, then every $3$-connected matroid $M\in\mathcal M$ having an $N$-minor has at most $k$ inequivalent $\mathbb F$-representations. In particular, if $N$ is uniquely representable over $\mathbb F$, then every such $M$ is uniquely representable over $\mathbb F$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a stabilizing minor has k inequivalent representations over a field, every 3-connected representable matroid containing that minor has at most k inequivalent representations. Unique representability therefore propagates from the stabilizer.
assumptions_latex: N\text{ is an }\mathbb F\text{-stabilizer for }\mathcal M
M\in\mathcal M\text{ is }3\text{-connected and has an }N\text{-minor}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \#\bigl(\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbb F}(M)/{\sim_{\mathrm{proj}}}\bigr)\le k;\qquad k=1\Longrightarrow M\text{ is uniquely }\mathbb F\text{-representable}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes field representability through maps whose span dimensions recover the matroid rank function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rank-$r$ matroid $M$ is $\mathbb F$-representable if and only if, for some $m\ge r$, there is a map $\psi:E(M)\to V(m,\mathbb F)$ such that $r_M(X)=\dim\langle\psi(X)\rangle$ for every $X\subseteq E(M)$. Such a map is an $\mathbb F$-coordinatization. Every coordinatization satisfies $\dim\langle\psi(E(M))\rangle=r$; consequently, $M$ is $\mathbb F$-representable if and only if it has an $\mathbb F$-coordinatization into $V(r,\mathbb F)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-r matroid is representable over a field exactly when its elements can be mapped to vectors so that the rank of every subset equals the dimension of the span of its images. The full image has span dimension r, so an r-dimensional ambient vector space suffices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is }\mathbb F\text{-representable}\iff\exists m\ge r\;\exists\psi:E(M)\to V(m,\mathbb F)\;\forall X\subseteq E(M),\ r_M(X)=\dim\langle\psi(X)\rangle,\quad\text{and }m\text{ may be chosen as }r.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hereditary classes, universal models, and varieties of simple matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions of matroid varieties and the matchstick and origami universal-model families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A collection \(\mathcal T\) of nonempty simple matroids is hereditary if every nonempty simple minor of each member lies in \(\mathcal T\), and the direct sum of any two members also lies in \(\mathcal T\). A sequence \((T_r)_{r\ge1}\subseteq\mathcal T\) is a sequence of universal models for \(\mathcal T\) if \(r(T_r)=r\) and every rank-\(r\) member of \(\mathcal T\) is a restriction of \(T_r\). A variety of simple matroids is a hereditary class having such a sequence. For \(n\ge1\), the matchstick models satisfy \(M_1(n)=U_{1,1}\), \(M_{2k}(n)=\bigoplus_{i=1}^k U_{2,n+1}\), and \(M_{2k+1}(n)=M_{2k}(n)\oplus U_{1,1}\); the corresponding variety consists of all their restrictions. The origami models satisfy \(O_1(n)=U_{1,1}\), and for \(r\ge2\), given a basis \(B=\{v_1,\ldots,v_r\}\) of \(V(r,\mathbb R)\), \(O_r(n)\) is the linear-dependence matroid on \(B\cup\{v_i+jv_{i+1}:1\le i\le r-1,\ 1\le j\le n-1\}\); its variety consists of all restrictions of these models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hereditary class of nonempty simple matroids is closed under nonempty simple minors and direct sums. Universal models are rank-indexed members whose rank-r model contains every rank-r member of the class as a restriction, and a variety is a hereditary class admitting such models. Matchstick models are direct sums of rank-two uniform matroids, with an additional coloop in odd rank; origami models arise by inserting n−1 represented points on each consecutive basis line. Their respective varieties consist of all restrictions of these models.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal T\text{ is a collection of nonempty simple matroids}
B=\{v_1,\ldots,v_r\}\text{ is a basis of }V(r,\mathbb R)\text{ for the origami construction}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal T\text{ is a variety iff it is hereditary and admits universal models }(T_r);\quad \mathcal M(n)=\{M:M\text{ is a restriction of some }M_r(n)\};\quad \mathcal O(n)=\{M:M\text{ is a restriction of some }O_r(n)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a simple uniquely \(\operatorname{GF}(q)\)-representable matroid and let \(k\ge r(M)\). If \(M\cong \operatorname{PG}(k-1,q)|T\), its \((\operatorname{GF}(q),k)\)-complement is \(\operatorname{PG}(k-1,q)\setminus T\). This complement is well-defined up to relabelling. Such complements exist for every simple binary matroid and every simple ternary matroid, but the complement of a uniquely \(\operatorname{GF}(q)\)-representable matroid need not itself be uniquely \(\operatorname{GF}(q)\)-representable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural and representability profile of P_8
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded consolidated profile of P_8; matrix entries omitted because the extracted display is incomplete.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: P_8\text{ is represented over }GF(3)\text{ by the matrix identified in the source. Its real geometric representation is obtained from a three-dimensional cube by rotating one face in its plane through }45^\circ\text{ about the center of that face. For every field }\mathbb F,\ P_8\text{ is }\mathbb F\text{-representable}\iff\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)\ne2.\text{ It is an excluded minor for }\mathbb F\text{-representability}\iff\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)=2\text{ and }\mathbb F\ne GF(2).\ P_8\text{ is dyadic and is an excluded minor for the near-regular and sixth-root-of-unity matroid classes. It is neither graphic, cographic, regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, nor a gammoid. It is self-dual but not identically self-dual, and its automorphism group is transitive on points but not on hyperplanes. It is not a tipless }4\text{-spike; every single-element contraction is isomorphic to }P_7\text{ and every single-element deletion is isomorphic to }P_7^*.\ P_8\text{ is base-orderable but not strongly base-orderable and is algebraic over every field.}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: P_8 is represented over GF(3) by the matrix identified in the source. Its real geometric representation is obtained by rotating one face of a three-dimensional cube through 45 degrees about that face's center. It is representable over a field F exactly when F does not have characteristic 2. It is an excluded minor for F-representability exactly when F has characteristic 2 and is not GF(2). It is dyadic and is an excluded minor for the near-regular and sixth-root-of-unity matroid classes. It is not graphic, cographic, regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, or a gammoid. It is self-dual but not identically self-dual, and its automorphism group is transitive on points but not hyperplanes. It is not a tipless 4-spike; every single-element contraction is isomorphic to P_7 and every single-element deletion to P_7^*. It is base-orderable but not strongly base-orderable and is algebraic over every field.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb F\text{ is a field whenever representability, excluded-minor status, or algebraicity is considered.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_8\text{ has the stated geometric and field representations, excluded-minor roles, class exclusions, duality, automorphism, minor, base-orderability, and algebraicity properties.}

knowledge_statements.title: Regular Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Field-independent finite matroid representability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite matroid \(M\) is regular if it is representable over every field. Equivalently, there exists a totally unimodular matrix \(A\), meaning every square subdeterminant of \(A\) belongs to \(\{0,1,-1\}\), whose column-dependence matroid is \(M\). Under this representation, reducing \(A\) over any field preserves exactly the same dependent and independent column subsets, so the represented matroid does not depend on the chosen field.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular matroid is representable over every field; equivalently, it has a totally unimodular matrix representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is regular if and only if \(M\) is represented by the columns of a totally unimodular matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Field-Dependence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characteristic-dependent representability illustrated by the Fano and non-Fano matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Matroid representability can depend on the characteristic of the field. The Fano matroid \(F_7\), whose seven elements are the nonzero vectors of \(\mathbb F_2^3\), is representable over a field \(\mathbb F\) if and only if \(\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)=2\). Its relaxation known as the non-Fano matroid \(F_7^-\) is representable over \(\mathbb F\) if and only if \(\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)\ne2\). Hence representability over one field neither implies representability over all fields nor depends only on field cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Fano matroid is representable exactly in characteristic two, whereas the non-Fano matroid is representable exactly outside characteristic two.
assumptions_latex: \(F_7^-\) denotes the standard relaxation of a circuit-hyperplane of \(F_7\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_7\) is \(\mathbb F\)-representable exactly when \(\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)=2\), while \(F_7^-\) is representable exactly when \(\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)\ne2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Induced representations and matroid representation stabilizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines representations induced on minors and stabilization of a matroid or class over a field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $A$ be an $\mathbb F$-representation of a matroid $M$. Deletion of an element is represented by deleting its column. If $e$ is not a loop, contraction of $e$ is represented by pivoting on a nonzero entry in its column and then deleting that column and the pivot row; all representations of $M/e$ obtained this way are projectively equivalent. If $I$ is independent, $I^*$ is coindependent, and $I\cap I^*=\varnothing$, the representations of $M/I\setminus I^*$ obtained by iterating these operations are said to be induced by $A$. A minor $N$ stabilizes $M$ over $\mathbb F$ if, whenever $N\cong M/I\setminus I^*$ under these conditions, any two $\mathbb F$-representations of $M$ that induce projectively equivalent representations of $M/I\setminus I^*$ are themselves projectively equivalent. If $\mathcal M$ is minor-closed and closed under duality, then $N\in\mathcal M$ stabilizes $\mathcal M$ over $\mathbb F$ if it stabilizes every $3$-connected member of $\mathcal M$ having an $N$-minor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deletion removes the corresponding representation column. Contraction of a nonloop pivots on a nonzero entry and removes the element's column and the pivot row; the possible results are projectively equivalent. Iterating deletion and contraction induces representations on suitable minors. A minor stabilizes a matroid when projective equivalence of the induced minor representations forces projective equivalence of the original representations. It stabilizes a minor-closed, dual-closed class when this holds for every relevant 3-connected member.
assumptions_latex: I\text{ is independent},\ I^*\text{ is coindependent},\ I\cap I^*=\varnothing
\mathcal M\text{ is minor-closed and closed under duality for the class-level definition}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N\cong M/I\setminus I^*,\quad \operatorname{Ind}_{I,I^*}(A_1)\sim_{\mathrm{proj}}\operatorname{Ind}_{I,I^*}(A_2)\Longrightarrow A_1\sim_{\mathrm{proj}}A_2;\qquad N\text{ stabilizes }\mathcal M\text{ iff it stabilizes every relevant }3\text{-connected }M\in\mathcal M.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent-set definition of a matroid, bases, and rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent-set axiomatization and the resulting base-equicardinality definition of rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a set and \(\mathcal I\subseteq 2^V\). The pair \((V,\mathcal I)\) is a matroid if (i) \(\varnothing\in\mathcal I\), (ii) \(I_1\subseteq I_2\in\mathcal I\) implies \(I_1\in\mathcal I\), and (iii) whenever \(I_1,I_2\in\mathcal I\) and \(|I_1|<|I_2|\), there exists \(k\in I_2\setminus I_1\) such that \(I_1\cup\{k\}\in\mathcal I\). For \(A\subseteq V\), a base of \(A\) is an inclusion-maximal member of \(\mathcal I\) contained in \(A\). All bases of \(A\) have the same cardinality, called the rank of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is a downward-closed set system containing the empty set and satisfying the exchange axiom. A base of a subset is an inclusion-maximal independent subset; the exchange axiom ensures that all such bases have the same size, which is the subset's rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Under the three independent-set axioms, }(V,\mathcal I)\text{ is a matroid, and every }A\subseteq V\text{ has equicardinal bases whose common cardinality defines its rank.}
