assumptions_latex: \(x_B+\sum_{j\in N}a_jx_j=b\), with \(x_B\) integer and all nonbasic variables nonnegative.
\(I\subseteq N\) indexes integer variables, \(C=N\setminus I\) indexes continuous variables, and \(f_0=\{b\}\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed Gomory mixed-integer inequality is valid for every mixed-integer solution of the tableau row.

notation.meaning: Integer and continuous nonbasic index sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized single-row Gomory mixed-integer cut under the stated tableau sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_j:=\{a_j\}\) for \(j\in I\). Every mixed-integer solution of the row satisfies \[\sum_{\substack{j\in I\\ f_j\le f_0}}f_jx_j+\frac{f_0}{1-f_0}\sum_{\substack{j\in I\\ f_j>f_0}}(1-f_j)x_j+\sum_{\substack{j\in C\\ a_j\ge0}}a_jx_j-\frac{f_0}{1-f_0}\sum_{\substack{j\in C\\ a_j<0}}a_jx_j\ge f_0.\] This is the normalized Gomory mixed-integer cut for the convention \(x_B+\sum_ja_jx_j=b\). It is violated by the associated basic solution in which all nonbasic variables vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-integer tableau row yields a piecewise-scaled inequality, using fractional parts for integer variables and signed coefficients for continuous variables, that cuts off the fractional basic solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Gomory Mixed-Integer Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed normalized mixed-integer cut is convention-dependent. Without a source fixing the tableau sign convention and normalization, its coefficient formula cannot be accepted reliably.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity and separation of a nonnegative-coefficient Gomory inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The variables \(\pi_i\) are only assumed nonnegative, not integer-valued. The isolated extract does not define \(f_0\), so its source notation is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\) be integer-valued and let \(\pi_i\ge 0\) satisfy \(y=\alpha_0+\sum_{i=1}^{\bar m}\alpha_i\pi_i\), where \(\alpha_i\ge 0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,\bar m\). Then every such \(\pi\) generating an integral value of \(y\) satisfies \(1\le f_0+\sum_{i=1}^{\bar m}\alpha_i\pi_i\), while the basic point \(\pi_i=0\) for all \(i\) violates the inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated integer-form equation with nonnegative parameters and nonnegative nonconstant coefficients, the displayed inequality is valid whenever y is integral and excludes the all-zero basic parameter solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 1\le f_0+\sum_{i=1}^{\bar m}\alpha_i\pi_i\text{ for every such }\pi\text{ generating integral }y,\quad\text{and this inequality fails at }\pi=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity and separation of the mixed-integer Gomory inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The fractional-part symbols \(f_i\), \(\bar f_i\), and the starred integer-part operator retain their source-defined meanings, which are not supplied in this isolated span.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\in\mathbb Z\) and \(\pi_i\ge0\) satisfy \(y=\alpha_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\alpha_i\pi_i\), with \(\alpha_0>[\alpha_0]^*\). Define \(I_1=\{i:f_i\le f_0\text{ and }\pi_i\text{ is integral}\}\), \(I_2=\{i:\alpha_i>0\text{ and }\pi_i\text{ is fractional}\}\), \(I_3=\{i:\bar f_i<f_0\text{ and }\pi_i\text{ is integral}\}\), and \(I_4=\{i:\alpha_i<0\text{ and }\pi_i\text{ is fractional}\}\). Then every such \(\pi\) generating integral \(y\) satisfies \(1\le \bar f_0^{-1}(\sum_{i\in I_1}f_i\pi_i+\sum_{i\in I_2}\alpha_i\pi_i)+f_0^{-1}(\sum_{i\in I_3}\bar f_i\pi_i-\sum_{i\in I_4}\alpha_i\pi_i)\), whereas \(\pi=0\) violates the inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a row with the stated nonintegrality condition and both integral and fractional nonnegative variables, the partition-dependent Gomory inequality is valid whenever y is integral and cuts off the all-zero basic solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 1\le \frac{1}{\bar f_0}\left(\sum_{i\in I_1}f_i\pi_i+\sum_{i\in I_2}\alpha_i\pi_i\right)+\frac{1}{f_0}\left(\sum_{i\in I_3}\bar f_i\pi_i-\sum_{i\in I_4}\alpha_i\pi_i\right)\text{ for every such }\pi\text{ generating integral }y,\quad\text{and it fails at }\pi=0.

children.title: Arithmetic-Family Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Containment, strength, and applicability relations among arithmetic cut families.

assumptions_latex: All cut families are compared for the same linear relaxation and the same declared integer variables.
Tableau rows are valid equations for that formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pure-integer fractional cuts admit Chvátal–Gomory interpretations, while single-row mixed-integer Gomory cuts are split cuts; converse statements require formulation qualifications.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-cut relationships under a fixed formulation, not equality of closures across arbitrary extended formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed pure-integer formulation, a Gomory fractional cut obtained from a tableau row can be represented as a Chvátal–Gomory cut after expressing that row as a valid aggregation of the formulation. For a fixed mixed-integer formulation, every single-row Gomory mixed-integer cut is valid for a split disjunction and hence belongs to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{split}}\). These statements compare generated inequalities, not unrestricted closures: reverse containments can fail for a fixed tableau, and changing or extending the formulation can change which tableau cuts are obtainable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pure-integer Gomory fractional cuts have Chvátal–Gomory interpretations, and single-row mixed-integer Gomory cuts are split cuts. Reverse comparisons depend on the formulation and available tableau rows.
knowledge_statements.title: Arithmetic-Family Comparisons

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The qualified family relationships are plausible and fit a comparison leaf, but they are nontrivial formulation-dependent claims. No inspectable comparison source is supplied to establish their precise scope.

children.title: Disjunctive Lift-Project Cut Family
children.top_down_role: Strengthening families derived from disjunctions and lifted reformulations.

children.title: Split Cuts
children.top_down_role: Strengthening structures derived from split disjunctions.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a polyhedron with integer-variable indices \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inequality valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(P\cap(D^0\cup D^1))\) is a split cut for the specified split disjunction.

notation.meaning: The two sides of the split disjunction.
The split hull associated with the disjunction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Split cuts for a mixed-integer relaxation using an integral primitive direction on integer coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Extend \(\pi\) by zeros outside \(I\), and define the split disjunction \[D^0:=\{x:\pi^{\mathsf T}x\le\pi_0\},\qquad D^1:=\{x:\pi^{\mathsf T}x\ge\pi_0+1\}.\] Every point satisfying the declared integrality lies in \(D^0\cup D^1\). The associated split hull is \[P^{\pi,\pi_0}:=\operatorname{conv}\bigl((P\cap D^0)\cup(P\cap D^1)\bigr).\] An inequality is a split cut for this disjunction if it is valid for \(P^{\pi,\pi_0}\); it cuts the relaxation when it is not valid for all of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A split disjunction excludes one open unit-width slab in an integral direction. Any inequality valid for the convex hull of the two remaining pieces is a split cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Split Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The split-disjunction and split-hull definition is standard and fits the definition leaf, but it lacks a cited source. The scope note also calls the direction primitive while the assumptions require only a nonzero integral direction; a source or explicit convention is needed to settle that discrepancy.

children.title: Disjunctive Cuts
children.top_down_role: Inequality families obtained from broader disjunctive structures.

assumptions_latex: \(D^1,\ldots,D^q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) satisfy every intended integer-feasible point belonging to \(\bigcup_{t=1}^qD^t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An inequality is a disjunctive cut when it is valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{t=1}^q(P\cap D^t))\) but not for all of \(P\).

notation.meaning: The alternatives of the valid disjunction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite valid disjunctions and cuts obtained from their convexified union.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D^1,\ldots,D^q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) form a valid disjunction for the intended integer-feasible set, meaning every such point lies in \(\bigcup_{t=1}^qD^t\). For a relaxation \(P\), define the disjunctive hull \[P_D:=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{t=1}^q(P\cap D^t)\right).\] An inequality \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) is a disjunctive cut generated by this disjunction if it is valid for \(P_D\). It is proper relative to \(P\) when some point of \(P\) violates it. Split cuts are the two-term special case arising from a split disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disjunctive cut is valid for the convex hull of the pieces obtained by intersecting a relaxation with every alternative of a valid finite disjunction.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-disjunction formulation is coherent, matches the plain statement, and has the correct definition role, but no source with a specific locator supports the selected convention for disjunctive cuts and properness.

children.title: Lift–Project Cut Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Lifted reformulation hierarchies followed by projection to the original space.

assumptions_latex: \(P^0=P\subseteq[0,1]^n\) is a relaxation of a binary-feasible set.
At each round, every coordinate split \(x_i=0\) or \(x_i=1\) is imposed and convexified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^{r+1}\subseteq P^r\), every binary-feasible point remains in every level, and \(P^n\) equals the binary hull.

notation.meaning: The relaxation after r lift–project rounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential coordinate-disjunction hierarchy; named lift–project systems may use stronger simultaneous operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q\subseteq[0,1]^n\), set \[L_i(Q):=\operatorname{conv}\bigl((Q\cap\{x:x_i=0\})\cup(Q\cap\{x:x_i=1\})\bigr).\] Define \(P^0:=P\) and, for \(r\ge0\), \[P^{r+1}:=\bigcap_{i=1}^n L_i(P^r).\] Then \(P^{r+1}\subseteq P^r\), and \(P\cap\{0,1\}^n\subseteq P^r\) for every \(r\). After at most \(n\) rounds, all coordinate disjunctions have been recursively convexified and \[P^n=\operatorname{conv}(P\cap\{0,1\}^n).\] This recursion provides a rank-indexed lift–project cut hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly convexifying every binary coordinate disjunction gives nested relaxations that retain all binary-feasible points and reach their convex hull within at most the number of variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Lift–Project Cut Hierarchy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record defines one particular coordinate-disjunction closure and asserts finite convergence to the binary hull after at most \(n\) rounds. That theorem-level conclusion is operator-sensitive and is not supported by a source. The representation content kind also understates the role of the finite-convergence claim; the appropriate kind must be settled together with an authoritative hierarchy reference.

children.title: Disjunctive Strength Relations
children.top_down_role: Comparative containment and closure strength across the three families.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a polyhedron containing the integer-feasible set \(Q_I=Q\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\).
Every disjunction in each family is valid for \(Q_I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{C}_{\mathfrak D_2}(Q)\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{\mathfrak D_1}(Q)\).

notation.meaning: closure obtained by intersecting all relaxations induced by disjunctions in the family

review_flags: A precise authoritative locator for the disjunctive-closure inclusion is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares closure strength by inclusion of the underlying families of valid disjunctions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid disjunction \(D=\bigcup_{j=1}^{k_D}D_j\), set \(T_D(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(Q\cap D)\), and for a family \(\mathfrak D\) define \(\mathcal{C}_{\mathfrak D}(Q)=\bigcap_{D\in\mathfrak D}T_D(Q)\). If \(\mathfrak D_1\subseteq\mathfrak D_2\), then \[Q_I\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{\mathfrak D_2}(Q)\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{\mathfrak D_1}(Q)\subseteq Q.\] Thus enlarging the disjunction family cannot weaken its closure; equality may occur when the added disjunctions contribute no further restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closure using every disjunction from a larger family is at least as strong as one using a subfamily.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Strength Relations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closure-inclusion property is mathematically coherent and the property content kind fits the leaf, but the record has no inspectable citation. A source specifically supporting disjunctive closures and the reversal of inclusion under enlargement of the disjunction family is required.

children.title: Closure Rank-Convergence Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Structural organization of repeated closure operations and their distance from the integer hull.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Shortest-Path Closure of a Distance Matrix
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines metric closure and states its triangle inequality and all-pairs shortest-path complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an n\times n distance matrix D=(d_{ij}), let \bar d_{ij} be the length of a shortest i\text{-}j path in the complete graph on \{1,\ldots,n\} whose edge \{i,j\} has length d_{ij}. Then \bar D=(\bar d_{ij}) is the closure of D. It satisfies \bar d_{ik}\le \bar d_{ij}+\bar d_{jk} for all i,j,k and can be computed in O(n^3) time by the Floyd\text{-}Warshall algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closure of a distance matrix replaces each entry by the corresponding shortest-path distance in the complete weighted graph. The resulting matrix satisfies the triangle inequality and is computable in cubic time by Floyd–Warshall.
assumptions_latex: \bar d_{ij}=\operatorname{dist}_D(i,j)\text{ in the complete weighted graph on }\{1,\ldots,n\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar d_{ik}\le \bar d_{ij}+\bar d_{jk}\quad\forall i,j,k,\qquad \bar D\text{ is computable in }O(n^3)\text{ time}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directed-Graph Closure and Maximum-Weight Closure Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines both feasible closures and the associated node-weight maximization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G=(N,A)$ be a directed graph. A set $N_1\subseteq N$ is a closure if $i\in N_1$ and $(i,j)\in A$ imply $j\in N_1$. Given arbitrary node weights $w_i\in\mathbb{R}$, the maximum-weight closure problem is to choose a closure $N_1$ maximizing $w(N_1)=\sum_{i\in N_1}w_i$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closure of a directed graph is a node set containing every out-neighbor of each of its nodes. With arbitrary signed node weights, the maximum-weight closure problem seeks such a set having the largest total node weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_1^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}\left\{\sum_{i\in N_1}w_i: N_1\subseteq N,\; i\in N_1\land(i,j)\in A\Rightarrow j\in N_1\right\}.

children.title: Closure Rank
children.top_down_role: Iteration-depth measures for reaching a target strengthened region.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is a closure operator satisfying \(P_I\subseteq\mathcal C(Q)\subseteq Q\) for every relevant relaxation \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathcal C}(P)=\min\{r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}:\mathcal C^r(P)=P_I\}\), with value \(+\infty\) if the set is empty.

notation.meaning: integer hull of the initial relaxation
the r-fold iterate of the closure operator

review_flags: A closure-specific source is needed to certify the rank convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the number of closure rounds needed to reach the pure-integer hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal C^0(P)=P\) and \(\mathcal C^{r+1}(P)=\mathcal C(\mathcal C^r(P))\) for \(r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). The \(\mathcal C\)-rank of \(P\) is \[\operatorname{rank}_{\mathcal C}(P)=\min\{r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}:\mathcal C^r(P)=P_I\}.\] If no finite iterate equals \(P_I\), its rank is \(+\infty\). In particular, the rank is zero exactly when \(P=P_I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closure rank is the least number of closure rounds required to obtain the integer hull, or infinity if no finite round suffices.
knowledge_statements.title: Closure Rank

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally consistent and correctly includes zero and infinite rank, and definition is the appropriate content kind. The closure-rank convention nevertheless has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Iterated Closure Structure
children.top_down_role: Nested geometry produced by repeated closure operations.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is monotone and satisfies \(P_I\subseteq\mathcal C(Q)\subseteq Q\) whenever \(P_I\subseteq Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_I\subseteq P^{(r+1)}\subseteq P^{(r)}\subseteq P\) for every \(r\ge0\), and \(P^{(\infty)}=\bigcap_{r\ge0}P^{(r)}\).

notation.meaning: the relaxation after r closure rounds
the limiting intersection of all finite iterates

review_flags: A general closure-calculus source is required for the stated operator framework.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the recursive, nested structure common to valid cutting-plane closures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(P^{(0)}=P\) and recursively define \(P^{(r+1)}=\mathcal C(P^{(r)})\) for \(r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). Then every valid integer point survives every round and the iterates form a descending chain: \[P_I\subseteq P^{(r+1)}\subseteq P^{(r)}\subseteq P.\] The infinite iterate is defined by \(P^{(\infty)}=\bigcap_{r=0}^{\infty}P^{(r)}\). Finite convergence occurs precisely when some \(P^{(r)}\) equals \(P_I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated closure application creates nested relaxations containing the integer hull; their limiting closure is the intersection of all rounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Iterated Closure Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive iterates, descending inclusions, and limiting intersection are consistent with the stated contractive closure assumptions, and property fits the leaf. No source with a specific closure-calculus locator is supplied.

children.title: Integer-Hull Convergence
children.top_down_role: Structural behavior of closure sequences approaching the integer hull.

assumptions_latex: All coordinates are required to be integral, and \(P_I=\operatorname{conv}(P\cap\mathbb Z^n)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) such that \(P^{(r)}_{\mathrm{CG}}=P_I\).

notation.meaning: the r-th Chvátal–Gomory closure of P

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence of Chvátal–Gomory closures for rational pure-integer polyhedra.

source_refs.locator: 5.21 The integer hull and cutting planes p. 83

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P^{(0)}_{\mathrm{CG}}=P\), and let \(P^{(r+1)}_{\mathrm{CG}}\) be the Chvátal–Gomory closure of \(P^{(r)}_{\mathrm{CG}}\). Then the sequence reaches the integer hull after finitely many rounds: there exists \(r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) such that \[P^{(r)}_{\mathrm{CG}}=P_I.\] Equivalently, every rational pure-integer polyhedron has finite Chvátal–Gomory rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a rational polyhedron with all variables integral, finitely many Chvátal–Gomory closure rounds produce its integer hull.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Hull Convergence

source_witnesses.locator: 5.21 The integer hull and cutting planes p. 83

children.title: Rank Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Families exhibiting large closure depth or slow structural progress.

assumptions_latex: \(P_I\subseteq\mathcal C(Q)\subseteq Q\) for every relevant relaxation \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The existence of \(x^*\in\mathcal C^{r-1}(P)\setminus P_I\) certifies \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathcal C}(P)\ge r\).
review_flags: A closure-rank source is needed for this witness-certificate formulation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A surviving fractional point witnesses that fewer than the claimed number of rounds cannot suffice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To certify the lower bound \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathcal C}(P)\ge r\), exhibit a point \(x^*\) satisfying \[x^*\in\mathcal C^{r-1}(P)\quad\text{and}\quad x^*\notin P_I.\] Membership in the first set verifies that \(x^*\) survives the first \(r-1\) closure rounds, while nonmembership in \(P_I\) verifies that \(\mathcal C^{r-1}(P)\ne P_I\). Hence no iterate numbered below \(r\) reaches the integer hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noninteger-hull point surviving through round r minus one certifies that the closure rank is at least r.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank Lower Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Under the stated closure assumptions, a point outside the integer hull surviving round r-1 is a valid certificate of rank at least r, and certificate is the correct content kind for this formulation. The witness characterization has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Separation for Inequality Families
children.top_down_role: Algorithmic access to structured and exponentially large cutting families.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F=\{a_i^Tx\le b_i:i\in I\}\) is a rational inequality family defining \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
The query point \(y\in\mathbb Q^n\) is given in binary encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle returns either an index \(i\) with \(a_i^Ty>b_i\) or the assertion \(y\in P\).

notation.meaning: possibly exponentially large indexed inequality family
polyhedron defined by every inequality in the family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact strong separation for a rational, explicitly encoded inequality family.

source_refs.locator: * 6.4 Equivalence of Strong Optimization and Separation p. 174
Section 4.6. Separation and Optimization p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On input \(y\), a strong separation oracle searches the indexed family \(\mathcal F\). If it finds \(i\in I\) with \(a_i^Ty>b_i\), it outputs the violated inequality \(a_i^Tx\le b_i\); otherwise it outputs that \(y\in P\). When this procedure runs in time polynomial in the encoding lengths of \(y\) and the family data, \(\mathcal F\) is polynomial-time separable even if \(|I|\) is exponential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separation oracle either returns an inequality violated by the query point or certifies that every inequality in the family is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation for Inequality Families

children.title: Extended-Formulation Complexity Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Lifted representations, projections, compactness, and barriers to concise linear descriptions.

children.title: Lift-Projection Representation Interface
children.top_down_role: Higher-dimensional descriptions projecting to the original feasible region.

children.title: Lifted Descriptions
children.top_down_role: Higher-dimensional linear descriptions associated with a target region.

assumptions_latex: \(Q=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{n+k}:A x+B y\le d\}\) is a polyhedron for some \(k\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) is a lifted description of \(P\) exactly when \(P=\{x:\exists y,\ (x,y)\in Q\}\).

notation.meaning: target polyhedron in the original variables
polyhedron in original and auxiliary variables

review_flags: A precise extended-formulation source locator is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a lifted linear description through coordinate projection onto the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The system \(A x+B y\le d\) is a lifted description, or extended formulation, of \(P\) when \[P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists y\in\mathbb R^k,\ A x+B y\le d\}.\] Equivalently, if \(\pi_x(x,y)=x\), then \(\pi_x(Q)=P\). The inequalities describe \(Q\) in the lifted space; equations may be included explicitly or represented separately without being counted as facet inequalities under the usual extension-complexity convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted description represents a polyhedron as the projection of a linear system containing auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Descriptions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection-based definition of a lifted description is mathematically consistent and definition fits the leaf. The additional convention about counting equations and facet inequalities also requires support, but no source is cited.

children.title: Projection Maps
children.top_down_role: Coordinate maps connecting lifted descriptions to original feasible regions.

assumptions_latex: \(\pi(z)=Tz+t\) is an affine map from \(\mathbb R^d\) to \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) represents \(P\) through \(\pi\) exactly when \(\pi(Q)=P\).

notation.meaning: affine projection or linear image map
matrix and translation defining the affine map

review_flags: A precise polyhedral-projection source locator is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Allows general affine images, including ordinary coordinate projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An affine map \(\pi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^n\), given by \(\pi(z)=Tz+t\), is a projection map from \(Q\) onto \(P\) when \[\pi(Q)=\{Tz+t:z\in Q\}=P.\] In the coordinate form \(z=(x,y)\), the standard projection is \(\pi_x(x,y)=x\). Surjectivity is required only after restricting the map to \(Q\); injectivity is not required, so several lifted points may represent the same point of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projection map sends every lifted feasible point into the target polyhedron and reaches every target point, without requiring a unique lift.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Maps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine-image condition is precise and the definition content kind fits the leaf. Because some sources reserve projection for coordinate or linear projections while using affine image more generally, an inspectable source is required for the stated terminology and representation convention.

children.title: Auxiliary Variable Spaces
children.top_down_role: Additional coordinate systems used to expose compact structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An auxiliary variable space is valid for a system \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times Y\) when \(\pi_x(Q)=P\).
review_flags: A source explicitly treating auxiliary spaces in extended formulations is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates original coordinates from variables introduced solely to obtain a compact formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An auxiliary variable space for \(P\) is a finite-dimensional space \(Y=\mathbb R^k\) whose coordinates supplement the original space \(X=\mathbb R^n\). A linear system defines \(Q\subseteq X\times Y\), and the auxiliary space is valid for that representation when \[P=\{x\in X:\exists y\in Y,\ (x,y)\in Q\}.\] The variables in \(Y\) need not have unique values for a given \(x\), and feasibility in \(P\) depends only on the existence of at least one lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary variables occupy an added space in which a linear system is built; existentially eliminating them recovers exactly the original polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary Variable Spaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The separation of original and auxiliary spaces and the existential projection condition are internally consistent, and definition fits the leaf. No source explicitly supporting this auxiliary-space formulation is supplied.

children.title: Lift–Projection Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Relationships among lifted dimension, description size, and projected geometry.

assumptions_latex: Extension size counts inequalities, while equations and auxiliary dimension are recorded separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{xc}(P)=\min\{m:\exists Q\text{ with }m\text{ inequalities and an affine }\pi\text{ such that }\pi(Q)=P\}\).
review_flags: A precise extension-complexity source locator is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes the inequality-count benefit obtainable by lifting and projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The extension complexity of \(P\) is \[\operatorname{xc}(P)=\min\{m:\exists Q=\{z:Cz\le d,\ Ez=f\},\ C\text{ has }m\text{ rows},\ \exists\pi\text{ affine},\ \pi(Q)=P\}.\] Hence any lifted description with \(m\) inequalities proves \(\operatorname{xc}(P)\le m\), whereas a lower bound on \(\operatorname{xc}(P)\) rules out every lift with fewer inequalities, regardless of its auxiliary dimension. A smaller projected description may therefore be obtained by accepting additional variables and equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extension complexity measures the fewest lifted inequalities needed to project onto a polytope, exposing the tradeoff between extra variables and inequality count.
knowledge_statements.title: Lift–Projection Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement gives the standard inequality-count interpretation of extension complexity and uses it to express the lift-projection tradeoff. Principle is acceptable for this tradeoff leaf, although the displayed formula itself is definitional. A precise extension-complexity source and locator are missing.

children.title: Decomposition-Based Formulations
children.top_down_role: Extended descriptions assembled from separable or compositional structure.

assumptions_latex: \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_i x\le b_i\}\) are nonempty polyhedra for \(i=1,\ldots,k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection onto \(x\) of the homogenized block formulation equals \(P\).

notation.meaning: scaled copy of the component-i point
convex hull of the component union

review_flags: A source for the disjunctive decomposition formulation and its recession assumptions is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convex-hull decomposition using one homogenized block per component polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every \(P_i\) is a polytope, then \(P\) is the projection onto \(x\) of \[x=\sum_{i=1}^k x^i,\qquad A_i x^i\le b_i\lambda_i\ \ (i=1,\ldots,k),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i=1,\qquad \lambda_i\ge0.\] Indeed, positive \(\lambda_i\) scale points of \(P_i\), while zero-weight blocks contribute only zero because the component recession cones are trivial. Thus the lifted system composes separate component descriptions into a formulation of their convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex hull of finitely many polytopes is represented by scaled component formulations whose nonnegative weights sum to one.
knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition-Based Formulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed homogenized formulation is valid under the statement's stronger condition that every component is a polytope, and representation fits the leaf. The formal assumptions instead introduce general nonempty polyhedra, for which recession behavior requires additional conditions or a more general formulation. The requested source is necessary to settle and document the intended scope.

children.title: Dynamic-Programming Formulations
children.top_down_role: Extended descriptions derived from finite state-space representations.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) is a finite acyclic directed graph with source \(s\) and sink \(t\).
Each arc \(a\in A\) has a label \(\ell_a\in\mathbb R^n\), and feasible objects correspond to \(s\)-\(t\) paths.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection of the unit \(s\)-\(t\) flow polytope under \(x=\sum_{a\in A}\ell_a f_a\) is the convex hull of path-label vectors.

notation.meaning: unit flow variable on arc a
arc label contributing to the represented object

review_flags: A source for the dynamic-programming network formulation is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents an acyclic dynamic program through its state-transition flow polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b_s=1\), \(b_t=-1\), and \(b_v=0\) for \(v\notin\{s,t\}\). Define the lifted system \[Bf=b,\qquad f\ge0,\qquad x=\sum_{a\in A}\ell_a f_a.\] Because the unit \(s\)-\(t\) flow polytope of an acyclic graph is the convex hull of incidence vectors of \(s\)-\(t\) paths, its projection is \[\operatorname{conv}\left\{\sum_{a\in p}\ell_a:p\text{ is an }s\text{-}t\text{ path in }G\right\}.\] Thus states and transitions yield an extended formulation for the dynamic program's feasible-output polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An acyclic dynamic program becomes a unit-flow formulation whose projection is the convex hull of vectors encoded by source-to-sink paths.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic-Programming Formulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The path-flow projection is the appropriate representation for an acyclic dynamic program, and representation fits the leaf. The sign convention for the node-arc incidence matrix must be specified to justify the stated supply vector, and no source for the network-flow formulation or path decomposition is cited.

children.title: State-Transition Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral encodings of state transitions underlying dynamic programs.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Transition Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Layered acyclic state-transition formulation and its projection onto accumulated decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a layered acyclic digraph with source \(s\), sink \(t\), and arc labels \(g_a\in\mathbb{R}^n\). The state-transition polyhedron is \[Q(D)=\left\{y\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{A}:\sum_{a\in\delta^+(v)}y_a-\sum_{a\in\delta^-(v)}y_a=b_v\quad(v\in V)\right\},\] where \(b_s=1\), \(b_t=-1\), and \(b_v=0\) otherwise. Under the projection \(x=\sum_{a\in A}g_a y_a\), its image is \[\operatorname{conv}\left\{\sum_{a\in P}g_a:P\text{ is an }s\text{-}t\text{ path in }D\right\}.\] Thus feasible paths encode discrete objects while flow variables provide an extended formulation of their convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unit-flow polyhedron on a layered acyclic state graph projects to the convex hull of the decision vectors encoded by source-to-sink paths.
assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite layered acyclic digraph with designated vertices \(s,t\).
Each arc \(a\in A\) has a label \(g_a\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\left\{\sum_{a\in A}g_a y_a:y\in Q(D)\right\}=\operatorname{conv}\left\{\sum_{a\in P}g_a:P\text{ is an }s\text{-}t\text{ path}\right\}.\)

notation.meaning: Unit source-to-sink flow polyhedron of the state graph.
Arcs leaving and entering vertex v.
Decision contribution attached to arc a.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically coherent for a finite acyclic state graph, and the content kind fits the leaf. However, the record cites no source. The local inventory contains general network-flow material but no cited locator supporting the path-flow projection statement in this state-space formulation context.

children.title: Composition Size Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Description-size consequences of decomposition width or state-space growth.

knowledge_statements.title: Composition Size Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive size under serial composition and multiplicative state growth under synchronous product composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For layered state graphs \(D_1,\ldots,D_k\), serial composition obtained by identifying consecutive terminal and initial states has \[|A|=\sum_{i=1}^k |A_i|\quad\text{and}\quad |V|\leq\sum_{i=1}^k|V_i|.\] By contrast, a synchronous product whose layer \(j\) stores every tuple of component states has at most \(\prod_{i=1}^k |V_{i,j}|\) states in that layer and at most \(\prod_{i=1}^k |A_{i,j}|\) simultaneous transitions between consecutive layers. Consequently, serially composable subproblems yield additive formulation size, whereas retaining all joint component states can produce multiplicative, hence exponential-in-\(k\), size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Serial state-space composition has additive size, while synchronous composition may multiply component state and transition counts, becoming exponential in the number of components.
assumptions_latex: Each \(D_i=(V_i,A_i)\) is a finite layered state graph.
Synchronous transitions are tuples of component transitions occurring in the same layer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|A_{\mathrm{serial}}|=\sum_i|A_i|\), whereas \(|V_{\mathrm{sync},j}|\leq\prod_i|V_{i,j}|\) and \(|A_{\mathrm{sync},j}|\leq\prod_i|A_{i,j}|\).\)

notation.meaning: States of component i in layer j.
Transitions of component i leaving layer j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the tradeoff leaf, and the additive and product counts are plausible under the stated serial and synchronous constructions. A source is required because the precise composition operations, size convention, and conditions behind exponential growth are model-dependent.

children.title: Symmetry in Extended Formulations
children.top_down_role: Effects of invariance requirements and symmetry breaking on lifted descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry in Extended Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivariance condition for a lifted formulation under a group acting on the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act linearly on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(gP=P\) for every \(g\in G\). An extension \((Q,\pi)\), with \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(\pi(Q)=P\), is \(G\)-symmetric if for every \(g\in G\) there exists an affine automorphism \(\widetilde g\) of \(Q\) such that \[\pi(\widetilde g(y))=g\pi(y)\qquad(y\in Q).\] Requiring this equivariance restricts the admissible extensions; a symmetry-breaking formulation may still project to \(P\) but need not admit compatible lifts \(\widetilde g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended formulation is symmetric when every original-space symmetry lifts to an affine automorphism commuting with projection; symmetry breaking removes this requirement.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite group acting linearly on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((Q,\pi)\text{ is }G\text{-symmetric}\iff(\forall g\in G)(\exists\widetilde g\in\operatorname{AffAut}(Q))\;\pi\circ\widetilde g=g\circ\pi.\)

notation.meaning: Symmetry group acting on the represented polytope.
Affine lift of the action of g to the extension.
Projection from the lifted space to the original space.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equivariance condition matches the stated topic and the condition content kind is appropriate. No citation or inspectable locator is supplied for this particular affine-automorphism definition of a symmetric extension.

children.title: Extension Complexity-Nonnegative Rank Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Measures and representation correspondences governing compact lifts.

children.title: Extension Complexity
children.top_down_role: Size measures for linear extended formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Extension Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facet-count definition for nonempty polytopes, allowing equations without charging them as inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty polytope \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), an extended formulation is a finite linear system \[Q=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^d:Ey=f,\;Gy\leq h\}\] together with an affine map \(\pi:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(\pi(Q)=P\). Its size is the number of inequalities, after redundant inequalities are removed; equations are not counted. The extension complexity of \(P\) is \[\operatorname{xc}(P)=\min\{\text{number of inequalities in an extended formulation of }P\}.\] Equivalently, the minimum may be taken over extensions \(Q\) and counts the facets of \(Q\) relative to its affine hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extension complexity is the minimum number of inequalities in any higher-dimensional polyhedron that projects affinely onto the given nonempty polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{xc}(P)=\min\{|I|:P=\pi(\{y:Ey=f,\;G_Iy\leq h_I\})\}.\)

notation.meaning: Affine projection realizing P as the image of Q.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is locally appropriate and clearly states that equations are not charged. It still requires an authoritative citation with a specific definition, section, theorem, or page locator; none is attached.

children.title: Nonnegative Rank
children.top_down_role: Nonnegative factorization complexity associated with polyhedral slack structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative Rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factorization definition over the nonnegative reals, including the zero-matrix convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a matrix \(M\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{p\times q}\), its nonnegative rank is \[\operatorname{rank}_{+}(M)=\min\left\{r\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}:M=TU,\;T\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{p\times r},\;U\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{r\times q}\right\}.\] Equivalently, it is the least \(r\) for which there exist nonnegative vectors \(t_1,\ldots,t_r\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{p}\) and \(u_1,\ldots,u_r\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{q}\) satisfying \(M=\sum_{k=1}^{r}t_k u_k^{\mathsf T}\). The convention \(\operatorname{rank}_{+}(0)=0\) is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonnegative rank of a nonnegative matrix is the smallest inner dimension of a factorization into two entrywise nonnegative matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}_{+}(M)=\min\{r:M=TU,\;T\geq0,\;U\geq0\}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The factorization definition and zero-matrix convention are precise, and definition is the correct content kind. The record has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Slack-Matrix Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural links between lifted descriptions and nonnegative factorizations.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty polytope containing at least two points.
\(P=\{x\in\operatorname{aff}(P):Ax\leq b\}\) is an irredundant relative-facet description, and \(v_1,\ldots,v_q\) are all vertices of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{xc}(P)=\operatorname{rank}_{+}(S)\), where \(S_{ij}=b_i-A_iv_j\).

notation.meaning: Row normal of relative-facet inequality i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Yannakakis correspondence for nonempty polytopes that are not singletons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polytope with at least two points, and write \[P=\{x\in\operatorname{aff}(P):Ax\leq b\},\] where the rows give an irredundant description by all facets relative to \(\operatorname{aff}(P)\). Let \(v_1,\ldots,v_q\) be all vertices of \(P\), and define the slack matrix \(S\) by \(S_{ij}=b_i-A_i v_j\). Then \[\operatorname{xc}(P)=\operatorname{rank}_{+}(S).\] The value is invariant under positive row scaling, vertex ordering, and the chosen irredundant relative-facet description. Hence the minimum inequality size of a lift equals the minimum inner dimension of a nonnegative factorization of its slack matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every nontrivial polytope, extension complexity equals the nonnegative rank of any irredundant relative-facet-versus-vertex slack matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Matrix Correspondence

children.title: Correspondence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Representation settings requiring qualifications to the standard complexity connection.

knowledge_statements.title: Correspondence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of the unmodified polytope slack-matrix equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The equality \(\operatorname{xc}(P)=\operatorname{rank}_{+}(S)\) in its facet-versus-vertex form presupposes a nonempty polytope with vertices and a finite relative-facet description. It does not apply verbatim to an unbounded polyhedron, because vertices alone do not encode recession directions; an appropriate generalized slack matrix must also represent extreme rays. Degenerate zero-dimensional cases require a separate convention because their slack matrix can be empty or zero while formulation-size conventions may count no inequalities. Likewise, adding redundant rows or nonvertex columns preserves the represented polytope but changes the matrix presentation, so invariance claims require the corresponding rows or columns to be redundant in the factorization sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The basic correspondence needs a bounded nontrivial polytope; unbounded sets require recession data, and zero-dimensional or redundant presentations require explicit conventions.
assumptions_latex: The basic correspondence uses a facet-versus-vertex slack matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ unbounded}\Rightarrow\text{vertex slacks alone do not determine the full extension problem};\quad \dim P=0\Rightarrow\text{a separate size convention is required}.\)

notation.meaning: Slack matrix used in the polytope correspondence.
Recession cone of an unbounded polyhedron P.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind fits the leaf, but the claims about generalized slack matrices for unbounded polyhedra, recession-ray data, zero-dimensional conventions, and redundant presentations are convention-sensitive. No source is supplied from which the exact boundary statement can be verified.

children.title: Compact Formulation Size-Bound Family
children.top_down_role: Constructive compactness results and barriers to concise formulations.

children.title: Compact Formulation Constructions
children.top_down_role: Structural families admitting concise extended descriptions.

assumptions_latex: \(Q=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^d:Ey=f,\;Gy\leq h\}\) is an integral polytope with \(m\) inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(X)\) and \(\operatorname{xc}(\operatorname{conv}(X))\leq m\).

notation.meaning: Finite family of feasible discrete vectors.
Affine decoding map from the lifted space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction principle for deriving small lifts from exact integral encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be finite, and let \[Q=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^d:Ey=f,\;Gy\leq h\}\] be an integral polytope described using \(m\) inequalities. Suppose an affine map \(\pi:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(\pi(Q\cap\mathbb{Z}^d)=X\). Then \[\pi(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(X)\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{xc}(\operatorname{conv}(X))\leq m.\] Network-flow, dynamic-programming, and decomposition constructions can instantiate this principle by providing a compact integral lifted polytope and an affine decoding map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact integral lifted polytope whose integer points decode exactly to the feasible discrete vectors gives an extended formulation of their convex hull, with size bounded by its inequality count.
knowledge_statements.title: Compact Formulation Constructions

children.title: Formulation Size Upper Bounds
children.top_down_role: Quantitative compactness guarantees for explicit formulation families.

knowledge_statements.title: Formulation Size Upper Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper bounds obtained by exhibiting a valid lifted linear description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polytope. If there exist matrices and vectors defining \[Q=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^d:Ey=f,\;Gy\leq h\}\] and an affine map \(\pi\) such that \(\pi(Q)=P\), then \[\operatorname{xc}(P)\leq \#\operatorname{rows}(G).\] Therefore, for a family \((P_n)\), an explicit construction with at most \(f(n)\) inequalities proves \(\operatorname{xc}(P_n)\leq f(n)\). The count concerns inequalities rather than auxiliary variables or equations, although those quantities may be reported separately when measuring the encoding length of an implementable formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any explicit lift with m inequalities proves that extension complexity is at most m; a family of such lifts supplies an asymptotic upper bound.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is a polyhedron satisfying \(\pi(Q)=P\) for an affine map \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{xc}(P)\leq\#\operatorname{rows}(G)\).

notation.meaning: Member n of a polytope family.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The claim is a direct upper-bound consequence of the stated extension-complexity convention, and complexity_bound is the correct role for this leaf. No authoritative source with a specific locator is cited.

children.title: Formulation Size Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Quantitative barriers to concise linear descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Formulation Size Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounds transferred from nonnegative-rank bounds on slack matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a nonempty polytope with at least two points and slack matrix \(S\). Any proof that every nonnegative factorization \(S=TU\) has inner dimension at least \(L\) establishes \[\operatorname{xc}(P)=\operatorname{rank}_{+}(S)\geq L.\] For a family \((P_n)\), a bound \(\operatorname{rank}_{+}(S_n)\geq f(n)\) rules out every extended formulation of \(P_n\) having fewer than \(f(n)\) inequalities, independently of the number of auxiliary variables. Thus nonnegative-rank arguments provide formulation-size lower bounds against arbitrary linear lifts, not merely a prescribed formulation template.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower bound on the nonnegative rank of a polytope's slack matrix rules out every linear extended formulation with fewer inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty polytope with at least two points.
\(S\) is a facet-versus-vertex slack matrix of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}_{+}(S)\geq L\Rightarrow\operatorname{xc}(P)\geq L.\)

notation.meaning: Proposed lower bound on factorization dimension.
Slack matrix of the nth polytope in a family.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-bound transfer is mathematically aligned with the nonnegative-rank correspondence, and complexity_bound fits the leaf. It depends on the uncited Yannakakis correspondence and has no independent authoritative locator.

children.title: Compactness Separation Results
children.top_down_role: Contrasts between classes with compact lifts and classes requiring large formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Compactness Separation Results
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal separation between small original-space descriptions and small lifted descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a polytope \(P\), let \(\operatorname{fc}(P)\) denote the minimum number of inequalities in any description of \(P\) within its own affine hull. Always \[\operatorname{xc}(P)\leq\operatorname{fc}(P),\] because \(P\) itself is an admissible extension. A family \((P_n)\) exhibits a compactness separation when \(\operatorname{fc}(P_n)\) and \(\operatorname{xc}(P_n)\) have asymptotically different growth; for example, \(\operatorname{fc}(P_n)=2^{\Omega(n)}\) and \(\operatorname{xc}(P_n)=n^{O(1)}\). Such a result certifies that auxiliary variables yield polynomial-size lifted formulations despite exponentially large direct descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extension complexity never exceeds direct facet complexity, and a compactness separation occurs when lifts are asymptotically much smaller than every original-space description.
assumptions_latex: Direct descriptions and extensions count inequalities relative to their affine hulls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{xc}(P)\leq\operatorname{fc}(P)\); a separation family may satisfy \(\operatorname{fc}(P_n)=2^{\Omega(n)}\) and \(\operatorname{xc}(P_n)=n^{O(1)}\).\)

notation.meaning: Minimum original-space inequality count for P.
Minimum lifted inequality count for P.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inequality between lifted and direct formulation sizes is coherent under the stated relative-affine-hull convention, and property is an acceptable role for the separation leaf. The notation \(\operatorname{fc}\) and the term 'compactness separation' are not sourced, so their intended convention cannot be confirmed.

children.title: Relaxation Fractionality-Gap Boundary
children.top_down_role: Divergence between continuous relaxations and discrete feasible solutions.

children.title: Fractional Extreme Points
children.top_down_role: Nonintegral vertex structures appearing in continuous relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Extreme Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fractionality of vertices in a relaxation of an integer feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^n\) be a discrete feasible set and let \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a polyhedron satisfying \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\subseteq R\). A point \(x^*\in R\) is a fractional extreme point of the relaxation if \(x^*\) is an extreme point of \(R\) and \(x^*\notin\mathbb{Z}^n\). Equivalently, \(x^*\) cannot be expressed as \(x^*=\lambda u+(1-\lambda)v\) for distinct \(u,v\in R\) and \(0<\lambda<1\), yet at least one coordinate of \(x^*\) is nonintegral. Its existence proves that \(R\) is not an integral polyhedron and hence \(R\neq\operatorname{conv}(X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fractional extreme point is a nonintegral vertex of a polyhedral relaxation; its existence proves that the relaxation is not the integer hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\in\operatorname{ext}(R)\setminus\mathbb{Z}^n\Rightarrow R\text{ is nonintegral and }R\neq\operatorname{conv}(X).\)

notation.meaning: Polyhedral relaxation of the discrete feasible set.
Set of extreme points of R.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the fractional-extreme-point leaf, introduces the relaxation and integer set, and correctly distinguishes a nonintegral vertex from an integral extreme point. No authoritative polyhedral-integrality source or inspectable locator is cited.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to the polyhedra P_sub and P_cut as defined in the surrounding formulation context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: P_{\mathrm{sub}}\subseteq P_{\mathrm{cut}}. Moreover, there exist examples for which P_{\mathrm{sub}}\subsetneq P_{\mathrm{cut}}, and P_{\mathrm{cut}} can have fractional extreme points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: P_sub is contained in P_cut; the containment is strict in some examples, and P_cut can have fractional extreme points.

children.title: Integrality-Gap Measures
children.top_down_role: Quantitative comparisons between relaxation values and discrete optima.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Gap Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative and additive gaps for a minimization relaxation with positive integer optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_I\subseteq X_R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be integer and relaxed feasible sets, and let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). Define \(z_I(c)=\inf\{c^\top x:x\in X_I\}\) and \(z_R(c)=\inf\{c^\top x:x\in X_R\}\). When \(0<z_R(c)\le z_I(c)<\infty\), the multiplicative integrality gap is \(g(c)=z_I(c)/z_R(c)\). Whenever both optima are finite, the additive gap is \(\Delta(c)=z_I(c)-z_R(c)\ge0\). For an instance class \(\mathcal I\), its worst-case gap is \(\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}g_I\), restricted to instances satisfying the positivity convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The integrality gap compares the integer optimum with the relaxation optimum, either by their ratio or difference; a class gap is the supremum over admissible instances.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(c)=z_I(c)/z_R(c)\) and \(\Delta(c)=z_I(c)-z_R(c)\ge0\).

children.title: Gap Instance Families
children.top_down_role: Structured examples exhibiting persistent or large relaxation gaps.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap Instance Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete graphs witness the asymptotic factor-two gap of the standard vertex-cover LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the unweighted vertex-cover instance on \(K_n\), consider the relaxation \(\min\sum_{v}x_v\) subject to \(x_u+x_v\ge1\) for every edge \(uv\) and \(x_v\ge0\). The assignment \(x_v=1/2\) has value \(n/2\), and summing all edge constraints shows every relaxed solution has value at least \(n/2\). Every integral vertex cover of \(K_n\) contains at least \(n-1\) vertices. Hence \(z_R=n/2\), \(z_I=n-1\), and the ratio \(z_I/z_R=2-2/n\) tends to \(2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete graphs make the standard vertex-cover LP asymptotically a factor two too optimistic: its value is n/2 while the integer optimum is n−1.
assumptions_latex: The standard edge-constraint LP relaxation for unweighted vertex cover is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_I/z_R=2-2/n\to2\) as \(n\to\infty\).

children.title: Relaxation Exactness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions separating integral relaxations from genuinely fractional regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Exactness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness characterized uniformly over linear objectives for a bounded relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_I\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and finite, and let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polytope with \(X_I\subseteq P\). Then the relaxation is exact for every linear minimization objective precisely when \(P=\operatorname{conv}(X_I)\): \[\min_{x\in P}c^\top x=\min_{x\in X_I}c^\top x\quad\text{for every }c\in\mathbb R^n \iff P=\operatorname{conv}(X_I).\] Thus any point of \(P\setminus\operatorname{conv}(X_I)\) permits a separating linear objective whose relaxed value is strictly better than the integer value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded relaxation is exact for every linear objective exactly when it equals the convex hull of its integer feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty polytope containing \(X_I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}(X_I)\) if and only if all linear-objective optimum values agree.

children.title: Exponential Facet Complexity
children.top_down_role: Families lacking concise descriptions in their natural spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Exponential Facet Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Natural-space inequality descriptions can require exponentially many facets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_n\subseteq\mathbb R^{\binom n2}\) be the symmetric traveling-salesperson polytope, the convex hull of incidence vectors of Hamiltonian cycles of \(K_n\). For each nonempty proper \(S\subsetneq V(K_n)\), every tour satisfies the cut inequality \(x(\delta(S))\ge2\). For the standard nontrivial ranges of \(S\), these inequalities yield exponentially many distinct facets: the number is \(2^{\Omega(n)}\). Consequently, every irredundant linear inequality description of \(P_n\) in its original edge-variable space contains \(2^{\Omega(n)}\) inequalities, although extended formulations are a separate complexity measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The traveling-salesperson polytope has exponentially many facets in its natural edge-variable space, so no polynomial-size irredundant description exists there.
assumptions_latex: \(P_n\) is represented in the original \(\binom n2\) edge variables.
Descriptions use linear inequalities without auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{facets}(P_n)=2^{\Omega(n)}\), implying natural-space description size \(2^{\Omega(n)}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Membership Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity boundary for deciding membership in an explicitly encoded polyhedron family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a family of rational polyhedra \(\mathcal P=\{P_s\subseteq\mathbb R^{n(s)}\}\), indexed by binary strings \(s\), define \(\mathrm{MEM}_{\mathcal P}=\{(s,x):x\in\mathbb Q^{n(s)},\ x\in P_s\}\). The family has NP-hard membership if this language is NP-hard under polynomial-time many-one reductions, with input length equal to the binary encoding length of \((s,x)\). Membership hardness concerns exact rational membership; it does not by itself imply hardness of weak membership, which allows a prescribed numerical tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Membership is hard when deciding whether an encoded rational point belongs to an indexed polyhedron is NP-hard under polynomial-time reductions.
assumptions_latex: The index \(s\) and point \(x\) have finite binary encodings.
Membership is interpreted exactly over rational data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{MEM}_{\mathcal P}\) is NP-hard under polynomial-time many-one reductions.

children.title: Separation Hardness

knowledge_statements.title: Separation Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity boundary for producing a violated valid inequality or confirming membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an indexed family of rational polyhedra \(\mathcal P=\{P_s\subseteq\mathbb R^{n(s)}\}\), the strong separation problem takes rational \((s,y)\) and must either certify \(y\in P_s\) or return rational \((a,\beta)\) such that \(a^\top x\le\beta\) for every \(x\in P_s\) but \(a^\top y>\beta\). The family has NP-hard strong separation when a polynomial-time algorithm for this task would yield a polynomial-time algorithm for an NP-hard language, under the stated binary encoding model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong separation is hard when producing a valid inequality violated by a given point, or confirming membership, would solve an NP-hard problem.
assumptions_latex: The polyhedron index and query point are rationally encoded.
A separating inequality must have a rational finite encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong separation for \(\mathcal P\) is NP-hard in the binary encoding model.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a family of nonempty, bounded, well-described rational polyhedra for which the required polynomial encoding bounds are supplied to the oracle algorithms. In the rational bit model, strong separation over each \(P\in\mathcal P\) is polynomial-time oracle reducible to strong linear optimization over \(P\), and strong linear optimization is polynomial-time oracle reducible to strong separation. knowledge_statements.title: Empty Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empty feasibility regime for a finite linear inequality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), the polyhedron \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\) is empty when no vector satisfies all inequalities, equivalently \(P=\varnothing\). By the inequality form of Farkas' lemma, emptiness is equivalent to the existence of \(y\in\mathbb R_+^m\) such that \(A^\top y=0\) and \(b^\top y<0\). Such a multiplier is a finite certificate that the defining system is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedron is empty when its inequalities have no common solution; a nonnegative Farkas multiplier certifies this infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\varnothing\iff\exists y\ge0:\ A^\top y=0,\ b^\top y<0\).

children.title: Unbounded Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Recession structure and representation issues for unbounded regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unboundedness characterized by a nonzero recession direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\) be nonempty. Its recession cone is \(\operatorname{rec}(P)=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:Ad\le0\}\). The polyhedron is unbounded if and only if \(\operatorname{rec}(P)\) contains a nonzero vector. Equivalently, there exist \(x_0\in P\) and \(d\ne0\) such that \(x_0+td\in P\) for every \(t\ge0\). For a minimization objective \(c\), such a ray proves objective unboundedness below when additionally \(c^\top d<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty polyhedron is unbounded exactly when it has a nonzero recession direction; a cost-decreasing recession ray certifies an unbounded objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ is unbounded}\iff\exists d\ne0:\ Ad\le0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Dimensional Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedra whose affine hull is proper in the ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonempty polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is lower-dimensional in its stated ambient space when \(\dim(P)=\dim(\operatorname{aff}P)<n\). Equivalently, there exist \(a\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb R\) such that \(a^\top x=\beta\) for every \(x\in P\). If \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\), lower dimensionality means that some nontrivial affine equality is valid throughout \(P\), whether or not that equality appears explicitly among the input constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty polyhedron is lower-dimensional when its affine hull is a proper affine subspace of the declared ambient space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim(P)<n\iff\exists(a,\beta),\ a\ne0:\ a^\top x=\beta\ \forall x\in P\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Alternating Time and Bounded-Alternation Time Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines time-bounded ATMs, their acceptance semantics, ATIME, and the bounded-alternation classes \(\Sigma_i\mathrm{TIME}\) and \(\Pi_i\mathrm{TIME}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be an alternating Turing machine and \(T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\). It is a \(T(n)\)-time ATM if, for every \(x\in\{0,1\}^*\) and every sequence of transition choices, it halts within \(T(|x|)\) steps. In the configuration DAG \(G_{M,x}\), \(C_{\mathrm{accept}}\) is accepting; an \(\exists\)-configuration is accepting if at least one successor is accepting; and a \(\forall\)-configuration is accepting if both successors are accepting. The machine accepts \(x\) exactly when \(C_{\mathrm{start}}\) is accepting, and \(\operatorname{ATIME}(T(n))\) consists of languages accepted by such machines. For every \(i\in\mathbb N\), \(\Sigma_i\operatorname{TIME}(T(n))\) and \(\Pi_i\operatorname{TIME}(T(n))\) consist respectively of languages accepted by such machines starting in an \(\exists\)-state or a \(\forall\)-state and making at most \(i-1\) changes between the two state-label types along every computation path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A T(n)-time alternating machine halts within T of the input length on every computation path. Acceptance propagates backward through its configuration DAG by OR at existential states and AND at universal states. ATIME collects languages accepted within that bound; Sigma-i-TIME and Pi-i-TIME additionally start existentially or universally and permit at most i minus one label alternations on every path.

\forall x\in\{0,1\}^*\ \forall\text{ transition-choice sequences},\ M\text{ halts within }T(|x|)\text{ steps}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L(M)\in\operatorname{ATIME}(T(n));\quad L(M)\in\Sigma_i\operatorname{TIME}(T(n))\text{ or }\Pi_i\operatorname{TIME}(T(n))\text{ under the corresponding initial label and }\le i-1\text{ alternations.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Big-O, Big-Omega, Big-Theta, Little-o, and Little-omega
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic comparisons of functions from the natural numbers to the natural numbers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\). Then \(f=O(g)\) iff there exist \(c>0\) and \(N\in\mathbb N\) such that \(f(n)\le c g(n)\) for all \(n\ge N\); \(f=\Omega(g)\) iff \(g=O(f)\); \(f=\Theta(g)\) iff \(f=O(g)\) and \(g=O(f)\); \(f=o(g)\) iff for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists \(N_\varepsilon\in\mathbb N\) such that \(f(n)\le\varepsilon g(n)\) for all \(n\ge N_\varepsilon\); and \(f=\omega(g)\) iff \(g=o(f)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For natural-number-valued functions, big-O denotes an eventual constant-factor upper bound; big-Omega reverses big-O; big-Theta requires bounds in both directions; little-o requires an eventual upper bound by every positive constant multiple; and little-omega reverses little-o.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}f=O(g)&\iff \exists c>0\,\exists N\,\forall n\ge N:\ f(n)\le c g(n),\\ f=\Omega(g)&\iff g=O(f),\\ f=\Theta(g)&\iff f=O(g)\land g=O(f),\\ f=o(g)&\iff \forall\varepsilon>0\,\exists N_\varepsilon\,\forall n\ge N_\varepsilon:\ f(n)\le\varepsilon g(n),\\ f=\omega(g)&\iff g=o(f).\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the machine structure and the quantifier-dependent interpretation of its nondeterministic choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An alternating Turing machine has two transition functions and labels every internal state other than \(q_{\mathrm{accept}}\) and \(q_{\mathrm{halt}}\) by either \(\exists\) or \(\forall\). At an \(\exists\)-labeled state, acceptance requires an accepting continuation under at least one transition choice; at a \(\forall\)-labeled state, acceptance requires accepting continuations under all transition choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An alternating Turing machine has two possible transitions at each nonterminal step, while each internal state is labeled existential or universal. An existential state accepts when some successor accepts, whereas a universal state accepts only when every successor accepts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Acc}(C)=\begin{cases}\bigvee_{C'\in\operatorname{Succ}(C)}\operatorname{Acc}(C'),&C\text{ is labeled }\exists,\\[2pt]\bigwedge_{C'\in\operatorname{Succ}(C)}\operatorname{Acc}(C'),&C\text{ is labeled }\forall.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Computability via Absolute Approximation and Separation from Zero
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes polynomial relative-error computability of an input-dependent real number.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An input-dependent real number \(\rho\) is polynomially computable with relative error if and only if it is polynomially computable with absolute error and there is a polynomial auxiliary algorithm that decides whether \(\rho=0\) and, when \(\rho\neq0\), computes a positive lower bound for \(|\rho|\). It suffices instead that the auxiliary algorithm compute \(b\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0}\) such that \(\rho=0\) or \(|\rho|\geq b\); together with the absolute-error algorithm, an approximation with tolerance \(b/3\) permits deciding whether \(\rho=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial relative-error computability is equivalent to polynomial absolute-error computability together with a polynomial procedure for detecting zero and bounding a nonzero value away from zero. It is enough to compute a positive rational b such that the value is zero or has magnitude at least b; absolute approximation to error b/3 then distinguishes the cases.
assumptions_latex: \rho\in\mathbb{R}\text{ is determined by the given input}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho\text{ is polynomially computable with relative error}\iff\bigl(\rho\text{ is polynomially computable with absolute error and is polynomially separable from zero}\bigr)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial Computability with Absolute or Relative Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines polynomial computability of an input-dependent real number using a rational accuracy parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho\in\mathbb{R}\) be determined by a given input. It is polynomially computable with absolute error if, for every \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0}\), a rational \(r\) satisfying \(|r-\rho|\leq\varepsilon\) can be computed in time polynomial in the input encoding length and \(\langle\varepsilon\rangle\). It is polynomially computable with relative error if the same holds with \(|r-\rho|\leq\varepsilon|\rho|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An input-dependent real number is polynomially computable with absolute or relative error if every positive rational tolerance admits a rational approximation with the corresponding error guarantee, computable in time polynomial in the input length and the tolerance's encoding length.
assumptions_latex: \rho\in\mathbb{R}\text{ is determined by the given input}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists r\in\mathbb{Q}\text{ computable in }\operatorname{poly}(\langle\mathrm{input}\rangle,\langle\varepsilon\rangle)\text{ such that }|r-\rho|\leq\varepsilon\text{ (absolute) or }|r-\rho|\leq\varepsilon|\rho|\text{ (relative)}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal machine model for access to finitely many relational oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A \(t\)-tape, \(k\)-oracle Turing machine consists of a Turing machine \(T=(X,B,E,\Phi,\Psi,\Xi)\) whose last \(k\) tapes are oracle tapes for relations \(\Pi_1,\ldots,\Pi_k\), together with distinguished query states \(x_1,\ldots,x_k\). In state \(x_i\), the string \(\sigma\) on the \(i\)-th oracle tape is replaced, beginning at the current head position, by some \(\tau\) satisfying \((\sigma,\tau)\in\Pi_i\), while the other tapes and heads remain unchanged. The machine is specified by \((T;\Pi_1,\ldots,\Pi_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multi-oracle Turing machine has designated oracle tapes and query states. Entering query state i replaces the query on oracle tape i with any answer related to it by Pi_i, without otherwise changing tapes or moving heads. The underlying machine and its oracle relations specify the model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i\text{ replaces oracle-tape query }\sigma\text{ by some }\tau\text{ satisfying }(\sigma,\tau)\in\Pi_i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nondeterministic Turing-machine acceptance and running time
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a binary-branching nondeterministic Turing machine, its existential acceptance rule, and its uniform time bound over all computation branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nondeterministic Turing machine \(M\) has two transition functions \(\delta_0,\delta_1\) and a distinguished accepting state \(q_{\mathrm{accept}}\). On input \(x\), \(M(x)=1\) iff some sequence of nondeterministic transition choices reaches \(q_{\mathrm{accept}}\); if every choice sequence halts without reaching that state, then \(M(x)=0\). The machine runs in time \(T(n)\) if, for every \(x\in\{0,1\}^*\) and every sequence of nondeterministic choices, it reaches either a halting state or \(q_{\mathrm{accept}}\) within \(T(|x|)\) steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nondeterministic Turing machine branches between two transitions at each step. It accepts an input if at least one branch reaches the accepting state, rejects if every branch halts without accepting, and runs in time T when every branch halts or accepts within T of the input length steps.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ has transition functions }\delta_0,\delta_1\text{ and accepting state }q_{\mathrm{accept}}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M(x)=1\iff \exists\text{ a choice sequence reaching }q_{\mathrm{accept}},\qquad \operatorname{time}_M(x)\le T(|x|)\text{ on every branch}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the real-number decision-tree model and its weighted depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An algebraic computation tree for \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\{0,1\}\) is a binary decision tree whose leaves are labeled Accept or Reject; computation nodes form \(y_v=y_u\circ y_w\), where each operand is an input \(x_i\) or an ancestor-node value and \(\circ\in\{+,-,\times,\div,\sqrt{\phantom{x}}\}\); and branch nodes test \(y_u=0\), \(y_u\ge 0\), or \(y_u\le 0\), again using an input or ancestor value. Each input follows one root-to-leaf path. Operations \(+,-\) have cost zero and \(\times,\div,\sqrt{\phantom{x}}\) have unit cost; the tree depth is the maximum path cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An algebraic computation tree decides a Boolean function on real inputs using arithmetic or square-root computation nodes, sign or equality branch tests, and accepting or rejecting leaves. Addition and subtraction are free, multiplication, division, and square root cost one, and depth is the maximum cost of a root-to-leaf computation path.
assumptions_latex: y_u,y_w\text{ are inputs or values computed at ancestor nodes}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{depth}(T)=\max_{p\text{ root-to-leaf}}\sum_{v\in p}\operatorname{cost}(v),\quad \operatorname{cost}(+)=\operatorname{cost}(-)=0,\quad \operatorname{cost}(\times)=\operatorname{cost}(\div)=\operatorname{cost}(\sqrt{\phantom{x}})=1.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic One-Tape Simulation of a Two-Tape Machine
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An output-preserving one-tape simulation exists with quadratic running-time overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $A$ be an alphabet and let
\[
\Phi:\{0,\ldots,N\}\times(A\cup\{\sqcup\})^2\to\{-1,\ldots,N\}\times(A\cup\{\sqcup\})^2\times\{-1,0,1\}^2
\]
be a two-tape Turing machine. Then there exist an alphabet $B\supseteq A$, an integer $N'$, and a one-tape Turing machine
\[
\Phi':\{0,\ldots,N'\}\times(B\cup\{\square\})\to\{-1,\ldots,N'\}\times(B\cup\{\square\})\times\{-1,0,1\}
\]
such that, for every $x\in A^*$,
\[
\operatorname{output}(\Phi',x)=\operatorname{output}(\Phi,x)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{time}(\Phi',x)=O\!\left(\operatorname{time}(\Phi,x)^2\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every two-tape Turing machine can be simulated by a one-tape Turing machine over an extended alphabet. On every input, the simulator has the same output and at most quadratic running-time overhead.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists B\supseteq A\;\exists N'\;\exists\Phi'\;\forall x\in A^*:\ \operatorname{output}(\Phi',x)=\operatorname{output}(\Phi,x)\ \land\ \operatorname{time}(\Phi',x)=O\!\left(\operatorname{time}(\Phi,x)^2\right).
