children.title: Integrality-Gap Measurement
children.top_down_role: Structural comparison between fractional and integral objective quality.

assumptions_latex: For every instance \(I\) in a class \(\mathcal{I}\), a minimization relaxation has values \(0<z_{\mathrm{LP}}(I)\le z_{\mathrm{IP}}(I)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The class integrality gap is \(\operatorname{gap}(\mathcal{I})=\sup_{I\in\mathcal{I}}z_{\mathrm{IP}}(I)/z_{\mathrm{LP}}(I)\); additive gap is \(\sup_{I\in\mathcal{I}}(z_{\mathrm{IP}}(I)-z_{\mathrm{LP}}(I))\).

notation.meaning: integer and relaxation optimum values on instance I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative and additive conventions for positive-valued minimization instances.

source_refs.locator: Section 8. Linear Programming Interpretation and Relaxation Procedures p. 77
Section 1.3. Linear Optimization Problems p. 8

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization instance \(I\) with \(0<z_{\mathrm{LP}}(I)\le z_{\mathrm{IP}}(I)<\infty\), its multiplicative integrality ratio is \(\rho(I)=z_{\mathrm{IP}}(I)/z_{\mathrm{LP}}(I)\ge 1\). For an instance class \(\mathcal{I}\), the multiplicative integrality gap is \(\operatorname{gap}(\mathcal{I})=\sup_{I\in\mathcal{I}}\rho(I)\). When zero or signed objective values make this ratio unsuitable, an additive convention is \(\operatorname{gap}_{+}(\mathcal{I})=\sup_{I\in\mathcal{I}}\bigl(z_{\mathrm{IP}}(I)-z_{\mathrm{LP}}(I)\bigr)\). The convention used must therefore be stated with the instance domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The multiplicative integrality gap is the worst integer-to-LP optimum ratio; an additive difference is used when ratios are unsuitable.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Gap Measurement

source_witnesses.locator: Section 8. Linear Programming Interpretation and Relaxation Procedures p. 77
Section 1.3. Linear Optimization Problems p. 8

children.title: Gap-to-Recovery Relations
children.top_down_role: Connections between relaxation gaps and attainable discrete recovery quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-to-Recovery Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization form relating an LP-relative rounding guarantee to the integrality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_I\subseteq X_R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n_{\ge 0}\), and suppose both minima are finite and positive. Define \(z_I=\min\{c^\top y:y\in X_I\}\) and \(z_R=\min\{c^\top x:x\in X_R\}\). If a recovery map \(R:X_R\to X_I\) satisfies \(c^\top R(x)\le \alpha c^\top x\) for every \(x\in X_R\), where \(\alpha\ge1\), then \[z_R\le z_I\le c^\top R(x^*)\le \alpha z_R\] for every relaxation optimum \(x^*\). Consequently, the instance integrality gap \(z_I/z_R\) is at most \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any rounding map whose cost is at most alpha times its fractional input bounds the minimization integrality gap by alpha.
assumptions_latex: \(c^\top R(x)\le\alpha c^\top x\) for every \(x\in X_R\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_I/z_R\le\alpha\)

Define \(z_I=\min\{c^\top y:y\in X_I\}\) and \(z_R=\min\{c^\top x:x\in X_R\}\). When \(0<z_R\le z_I<\infty\), the instance-specific integrality gap is \(g(I)=z_I/z_R\). children.title: Rounding Method Regime Pair
children.top_down_role: High-level bridge from fractional solutions to discrete constructions.

children.title: Deterministic Rounding Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Discrete recovery based on fixed choices from fractional information.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Rounding Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic deterministic interface from a solved relaxation to an integral feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an instance \(I\), a relaxation \(X_R(I)\), an integral feasible set \(X_I(I)\subseteq X_R(I)\), and cost \(c\). Compute an optimal relaxed point \(x^*\in\arg\min_{x\in X_R(I)}c^\top x\). Apply a deterministic map \(R_I:X_R(I)\to X_I(I)\) and output \(y=R_I(x^*)\). The interface is an \(\alpha\)-rounding interface if, for every admissible instance, \[y\in X_I(I)\quad\text{and}\quad c^\top y\le\alpha c^\top x^*.\] It stops after the relaxation solver and \(R_I\) terminate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the relaxation, deterministically map its optimum to an integral feasible point, and require an alpha-relative cost guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(R_I\) terminates on every admissible relaxed optimum
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_I(x^*)\in X_I(I)\) and \(c^\top R_I(x^*)\le\alpha c^\top x^*\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the deterministic-interface leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied. The record also leaves the admissible instance class, cost-vector domain, and the usual condition \(\alpha\ge1\) implicit. An authoritative deterministic-rounding locator is required before the exact interface can be reviewed reliably.

children.title: Randomized Rounding Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Discrete recovery based on probability distributions derived from fractional information.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Rounding Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic randomized interface with almost-sure feasibility and expected approximation control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an instance \(I\), relaxed feasible set \(X_R(I)\), integral set \(X_I(I)\), and cost \(c\). Compute \(x^*\in\arg\min_{x\in X_R(I)}c^\top x\), sample internal randomness \(\omega\), and output \(Y=R_I(x^*,\omega)\). An \(\alpha\)-randomized rounding interface satisfies \[\Pr(Y\in X_I(I))=1\quad\text{and}\quad \mathbb E[c^\top Y]\le\alpha c^\top x^*.\] If only a success event \(S\) is guaranteed, the interface must state \(\Pr(S)\), its resampling rule, and whether the bound is conditional on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized rounding interface returns a feasible integral solution almost surely and controls its expected cost relative to the relaxed optimum.
assumptions_latex: The random map terminates almost surely
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr(Y\in X_I(I))=1\) and \(\mathbb E[c^\top Y]\le\alpha c^\top x^*\)

notation.meaning: Declared success event when feasibility is not unconditional

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the randomized-interface leaf and the almost-sure feasibility/expected-cost distinction is coherent, but there is no source. The probability space or random-seed domain and \(\alpha\ge1\) are also unstated. A precise randomized-rounding source is needed to validate the selected generic interface and its success-event addendum.

children.title: Rounding-Derandomization Relations
children.top_down_role: Connections between randomized constructions and deterministic counterparts.

knowledge_statements.title: Rounding-Derandomization Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-expectation conversion of sequential randomized rounding into deterministic rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a randomized rounding procedure be determined by finite choices \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\), and let \(L(B_1,\ldots,B_m)\) be an integrable loss. Suppose conditional expectations can be computed and every partial assignment has at least one next value \(b\) satisfying \[\mathbb E[L\mid B_1=b_1,\ldots,B_{k-1}=b_{k-1},B_k=b]\le \mathbb E[L\mid B_1=b_1,\ldots,B_{k-1}=b_{k-1}].\] Choosing such a value at each step produces a deterministic outcome with \(L(b_1,\ldots,b_m)\le\mathbb E[L]\). If zero loss of feasibility is encoded in \(L\), feasibility is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix each random choice without increasing conditional expected loss; the final deterministic loss is no greater than the original expectation.
assumptions_latex: The random procedure uses finitely many sequential choices
Required conditional expectations and minimizing choices are computable
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(b_1,\ldots,b_m)\le\mathbb E[L(B_1,\ldots,B_m)]\)

notation.meaning: Deterministically fixed value of the kth choice
Loss or pessimistic estimator being controlled

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-expectation relation is standard and the principle kind fits the leaf, but no source is supplied. Moreover, saying that zero feasibility loss is encoded in \(L\) does not by itself imply preservation: one needs a nonnegative feasibility penalty and an initial expected-loss bound forcing the final penalty to zero. The finite choice domains and conditioning on positive-probability partial assignments also require specification.

children.title: Comparative Rounding Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions favoring deterministic or randomized recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Comparative Rounding Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of deterministic guarantees, expected guarantees, and high-probability guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a relaxed optimum \(x^*\) and nonnegative cost, deterministic \(\alpha\)-rounding requires \(c^\top y\le\alpha c^\top x^*\) for its single output. Randomized expected \(\alpha\)-rounding requires only \(\mathbb E[c^\top Y]\le\alpha c^\top x^*\), which implies that some outcome in the support has cost at most \(\alpha c^\top x^*\) but does not itself identify that outcome. A high-probability \((\alpha,\delta)\) regime requires \[\Pr(c^\top Y\le\alpha c^\top x^*)\ge1-\delta.\] Neither an expectation guarantee nor existence of a good outcome alone supplies an efficient deterministic recovery rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deterministic, expected, and high-probability rounding guarantees differ in quantifiers and in whether a good outcome can be efficiently found.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[c^\top Y]\le\alpha c^\top x^*\Rightarrow\exists y\in\operatorname{supp}(Y):c^\top y\le\alpha c^\top x^*\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: comparison follows from guarantee quantifiers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind is suitable for comparing guarantee regimes, but no citation is supplied. For a general random output, an expectation bound guarantees an outcome of cost at most the expectation, while locating such a point in a topological support requires the support and cost regularity to be defined. The domain \(\alpha\ge1\) should also be explicit.

children.title: Iterative Relaxation Interface
children.top_down_role: High-level bridge from extreme-point structure to repeated fixing and relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterative Relaxation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract repeated solve–fix–relax scheme driven by extreme-point structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the residual instance \(I_0=I\) and partial integral solution \(F_0=\varnothing\). At iteration \(t\), solve the current relaxation and select an extreme optimum \(x^t\). A structural rule either fixes an integral decision from \(x^t\), updating \(F_{t+1}\), or removes or weakens a designated residual constraint, producing \(I_{t+1}\). Require every iteration to reduce a finite progress measure \(\mu(I_t)\). Stop when no variables remain, and output the completion determined by \(F_t\). Correctness requires the fixing rules to preserve extendability and the relaxation rules to account explicitly for any permitted objective or constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve an extreme-point relaxation, fix integral decisions or relax controlled constraints, and terminate when a finite progress measure reaches zero.
assumptions_latex: Each residual relaxation has an extreme optimum or reports infeasibility
Every update strictly decreases a finite measure \(\mu\)
Fixing and constraint-removal rules have declared invariants
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu(I_{t+1})<\mu(I_t)\) until a completed integral output is returned

children.title: Weak-Relaxation Failure
children.top_down_role: Relaxations whose fractional objective bounds provide little discrete guidance.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Relaxation Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete graphs witness the factor-two boundary of the basic vertex-cover relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimum vertex cover on the complete graph \(K_n\), consider the relaxation \[\min\sum_{v}x_v\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_u+x_v\ge1\ \text{for every edge }uv,\quad x_v\ge0.\] The assignment \(x_v=1/2\) has value \(n/2\), and summing all edge inequalities shows it is optimal. Every integral vertex cover has at least \(n-1\) vertices. Thus the instance gap is \((n-1)/(n/2)=2-2/n\), approaching \(2\). Consequently, this relaxation cannot support a uniform recovery factor strictly below \(2\) on all complete graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The basic vertex-cover LP has gap approaching two on complete graphs, preventing any uniformly better LP-relative rounding guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation contains only edge-covering inequalities and nonnegativity

notation.meaning: Fractional selection variable for vertex v

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical complete-graph vertex-cover gap example

knowledge_statements.scope_note: An odd-cycle fractional matching vertex defeats objective-preserving integral recovery.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 3. Elements of network optimization p. 95

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For maximum-cardinality matching on the triangle \(C_3\), consider the degree relaxation \[\max\sum_e x_e\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{e\ni v}x_e\le1\ \text{for every vertex }v,\quad x_e\ge0.\] The fractional point \(x_e=1/2\) for all three edges is feasible and has value \(3/2\); summing the degree constraints shows it is optimal. Every integral matching contains at most one edge and therefore has value \(1\). Hence no recovery map from this optimum can preserve its objective value. The valid odd-set inequality \(\sum_{e\in E(C_3)}x_e\le1\) removes this fractional optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The triangle's half-integral degree-relaxation optimum exceeds every integral matching, so objective-preserving recovery is impossible; the triangle odd-set inequality removes this fractional optimum.

children.title: Recovery-Quality Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on the discrete quality recoverable from fractional solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Recovery-Quality Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An integrality gap is a lower bound on every relaxation-relative recovery factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_I\subseteq X_R\), let \(c\ge0\), and define positive finite minimization optima \(z_I\) and \(z_R\). For any map \(R:X_R\to X_I\) and any relaxed optimum \(x^*\), feasibility gives \(c^\top R(x^*)\ge z_I\). Therefore, if \(R\) claims \(c^\top R(x^*)\le\alpha z_R\), then necessarily \[\alpha\ge\frac{z_I}{z_R}.\] For a family \(\mathcal I\), every uniform relaxation-relative recovery factor is at least \(\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}z_I(I)/z_R(I)\). An unbounded family gap precludes every finite uniform factor based on that relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: No rounding method measured against a relaxation can guarantee a factor smaller than that relaxation’s worst-case integrality gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha\ge z_I/z_R\)

notation.meaning: Recovery map from relaxed to integral solutions

children.title: Roundability Threshold Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural transitions between recoverable and poorly recoverable fractional solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Roundability Threshold Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instance-family threshold defined by existence of a uniform LP-relative recovery map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization family \(\mathcal I\) with relaxation optima \(x_I^*\) and integral feasible sets \(X_I^{\mathrm{int}}\), call the family \(\alpha\)-roundable if there is one algorithm \(R\) such that, for every \(I\in\mathcal I\), \[R(I,x_I^*)\in X_I^{\mathrm{int}}\quad\text{and}\quad c_I^\top R(I,x_I^*)\le\alpha c_I^\top x_I^*.\] Its roundability threshold is \(\alpha^*(\mathcal I)=\inf\{\alpha\ge1:\mathcal I\text{ is }\alpha\text{-roundable}\}\). Relative to a declared computational model, efficient roundability additionally requires \(R\) to run in polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family’s roundability threshold is the infimum factor achieved uniformly by one feasible recovery algorithm, optionally under polynomial-time constraints.
assumptions_latex: Every instance has a finite relaxed optimum
The admissible algorithmic model is fixed
Costs and approximation factors use the minimization convention
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha^*(\mathcal I)=\inf\{\alpha\ge1:\exists R\ \forall I\in\mathcal I,\ c_I^\top R(I,x_I^*)\le\alpha c_I^\top x_I^*\}\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: formal threshold induced by approximation factors

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits a roundability-threshold leaf, but no authoritative source supports this terminology or the computational interpretation. The definition also fixes symbols \(x_I^*\) without saying whether the algorithm receives an arbitrary optimum, a canonically selected optimum, or may choose one through the relaxation solver; these alternatives can change the algorithmic condition.

children.title: Relaxation-Repair Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Stronger formulations or structural refinements used when basic relaxations fail.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Repair Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-and-resolve interface for repairing fractional obstructions before recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a relaxation \(P_0\supseteq\operatorname{conv}(X_I)\), cost \(c\), a separation routine for a chosen family of valid inequalities, and a recovery map \(R\). At iteration \(t\), compute \(x^t\in\arg\min_{x\in P_t}c^\top x\). If the separator returns a valid inequality \(a^\top x\le b\) violated by \(x^t\), set \(P_{t+1}=P_t\cap\{x:a^\top x\le b\}\). Otherwise apply \(R\) and output \(R(x^t)\) if integral feasibility and the declared quality bound hold. Stop on successful recovery, certified infeasibility, or a stated iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly separate violated valid inequalities, strengthen and resolve the relaxation, then round once the repaired solution meets the recovery conditions.
assumptions_latex: Every added inequality is valid for \(X_I\)
Optimization and separation terminate under the declared stopping rule
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{t+1}\supseteq\operatorname{conv}(X_I)\) and \(x^t\notin P_{t+1}\) after every successful repair
